#4157. Company of Heroes 3 Update Fixes Its Worst Mission

The big 2026 is almost over, and if you work at Relic Entertainment or are a Company of Heroes fan like me, it’s fair to say this year has been a strong one for the franchise.

The classic real-time strategy franchise has brought Company of Heroes 3 into maturity with update 3.0, and has dared to go beyond the battlegroup packs for the first time with not one but two DLCs that finally enhance single-player gameplay to a significant extent.

Battleplan is a real breakthrough for the strategy genre.

This Wednesday, just in time for the Thanksgiving break, Relic released the Operation Torch campaign DLC for Company of Heroes 3. The campaign has proven divisive, currently sitting with mixed Steam reviews and sparking either love or disappointment from critics.

One thing everyone seems to agree on, however, is that one mission in particular was a tough sell, and it looks like Relic Entertainment has gotten the hint.

The Operation Torch campaign DLC is a single-player-only affair that comes with fifteen hand-crafted missions, a nice change of pace from the mix of cinematics and random skirmishes that defined Relic’s previous attempts at solo play in Company of Heroes 3.

In our review, Jaime Tugayev exalts Operation Torch as “a blueprint for potential future DLCs that focus on telling stories, rather than just adding new units,” but you will also find plenty of disappointment about a mission so bad it was described as “playing Pac-Man” in that same review.

A more exasperated comment on Reddit goes as far as saying “they should fire whoever came up with that”, which feels a little extreme but shows just how big of a problem this was.

Titled Longstop Infiltration, the mission in question puts you in charge of a nighttime raid to disable German heavy guns on Longstop Hill ahead of a land assault. With the odds stacked against them, the commandos must sneak past German defences, plant explosive charges, and leave the area before the whole place goes up in smoke.

What sounds like a great action movie plot turned out to be a pretty mediocre gameplay experience due to mission design issues, so Relic Entertainment has taken steps to fix this.

As part of hotfix 3.0.4, the commando units in Longstop Infiltration have received boosts to both health and speed. This, the developers hope, will allow players to better use gaps between German patrols and also help the commandos survive engagements when they are triggered.

At the moment, these changes only apply to Easy and Standard difficulties, letting players with more masochistic inclinations enjoy the mission in its original form.

What sounds like a great action movie plot turned out to be a pretty mediocre gameplay experience due to mission design issues

Given how much negative feedback has been thrown Relic’s way over this particular mission, the change is a welcome one in the sense that it makes Longstop Infiltration doable by the average player. There are intrinsic mission design problems that remain, and part of me wonders if the DLC would have been better served had Longstop Infiltration been scrapped altogether.

Right now, the future for Company of Heroes 3 includes new battlegroups, maps for both skirmish and Final Stand modes, cosmetics, and multiplayer balancing patches.

The game received update 3.0 earlier this month, which Relic branded “the biggest release for Company of Heroes 3 since its initial launch.” You can read the gargantuan patch notes here.

From a single-player perspective, the biggest item there is the rebalancing of the campaign map emplacements, which before would always decimate infantry units moving about.

Company of Heroes 3 is available on Windows, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X/S.

Company of Heroes: Final Stand brings roguelike action to a realistic strategy game, and against all odds, it's good fun.

#4156. Grand Theft Auto VI Shatters Records, Making $3.79 Billion In 24 Hours As The Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever

Grand Theft Auto VI dropped yesterday to massive success, and while we expected it to do well, hearing the numbers behind the historic launch day is still staggering. According to a statement obtained by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier and IGN, Rockstar has confirmed that the open-world juggernaut made $3.79 billion in 24 hours. This makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time – it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and it's not especially close.

Schreier goes on to confirm that much of that money comes from GTA VI's record-breaking pre-orders. It turns out, there were 32.5 million pre-sales, which is a truly mind-bending number. For context, its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, currently the second best-selling game of all time, sold 11.21 million copies in the first 24 hours – GTAVI nearly triples that figure. In pre-orders alone, the game has become the 30th best-selling game of all time, with more copies sold in the first day than Elden Ring and Super Mario Odyssey have sold, period.

In terms of the dollar amount, GTAVI's $3.79 billion in 24 hours is not just more money than any film has made in its opening weekend; it's more money than any movie has ever made in the box office – even Avengers: Endgame, which currently holds the highest worldwide gross, is still shy of $3 billion after several successful theatrical runs.

Grand Theft Auto VI also set the record on Metacritic for the highest-reviewed game of all time (with an average critic score of 99), and it headlined this week's rollout of the Game Awards 2026 nominees, with more nominations than any other game. We also loved it, and our editor-in-chief Matt Miller scored it a perfect 10.

#4155. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4154. The Wrapp - Vampiric therapists, crabs, and cardboard Digimon

What are the Pocket Gamer team playing this weekend?

Hello! And welcome back to The Wrapp once again. If it's your first time in these parts, it's where we chat about our gaming plans for the next couple of days. This week, Jupiter has learned that anything can be a crustacean, Dann is still virtually globetrotting, and Shaun is hoping Bandai's latest Digimon mobile game isn't awful.

I have been playing Everything is Crab this week, as it’s newly out, and I have been enjoying the various combinations that you can end up with when playing. I also am back on the Duolingo train, for the next 3 days, as Duolingo is doing a collaboration with Pokémon Go where you can get some really adorable background Pokémon if you have a 7 day in a row streak. I really do hate Duolingo (not only because of their AI usage, but also because I do not believe the language courses actually teach you how to speak), so I cannot believe they collaborated with Pokémon and have forced me back in.

I’ll be busy burying myself in all the relaxing vibes of Petit Planet in the next few days, because it’s officially launching on December 4th just in time for the holidays! I’m reserving my thoughts for my review, of course - but suffice it to say it’ll be a cosy (perhaps too cosy?) weekend for me.

I’ve had a mix of excitement and disappointment over this week. Vampire Therapist turned out to be a really great little pick, but Postal Classic & Uncut, which I covered last week, was a bit of a stinker. It did give me a chance to talk about violence in video games, though, which is always an interesting topic.

Up ahead we’ve got the launch of Silver Palace coming soon, and I’m prepping for a trip to LA to witness more of Arknights: Endfield in action, particularly their 2.0 build! It’ll coincide with The Game Awards, which I’m not privy to attending, but I’m expecting some controversial picks. At least the mobile category looks pretty solid.

I have said this at every opportunity, and will continue to do so; Digimon Up was absolutely awful. I say that as both a judge of gameplay and a big fan of the IP. Even for an idle game, it had nothing to do. And no global passives for raising different Digimon? What was that about? Anyway, it blew. But what I am sure will not suck is Digimon Alysion.

The Digimon Card Game is one of my favourite TCGs, and I have been so excited to play the mobile version. I could never make a good Gabumon deck with the physical cards, so I can’t wait to reap my free packs and give it a go here. I am a big fan of the Memory gauge and the Digivolution mechanics. It won’t be bigger than Pokémon TCG Pocket, just on the strength of the IP, but it will definitely deserve to be, I have no doubt.

Not to be a broken record, but I’m still messing around with 80 Days in my spare time. I’ve really started to get into a groove now and have successfully circumnavigated the globe three times in a row, with the last two including successful trips to the North Pole. I do wish that there was an opportunity to travel around in a southward or westward direction, but I understand the reasoning. That said, maybe you can head southward? I’ve only come up through Africa, as every time I start heading in that direction I get involved in the dissent in Southern Europe and end up whipped up in the Venetian Issues.

Aside from this, I’m going to be playing a lot of Sol Cesto on my PC, in celebration of this week’s announcement that it's getting a mobile port. Sol Cesto had me completely hooked through its Early Access journey on PC, and I loved booting it up as new updates were pushed to it… The balance of risk and reward is exceptional, and it feels like a perfect fit for mobile; I’m excited to play it again.

It's been kind of a slow reveal on my end of things, not much to steal my gaze. Sure, I've got plenty of suggestions and related recommendations, but nothing that's biting down hard. I've still got Warhammer Survivors and Kingdom Rush Genesis to keep me entertained (still on the fence with Booster Pack Heroes). Though, there's still time before the weekend is out and I can spare a few minutes to do a quick search, and I got something…

Whether I searched or it was right there when I opened the store is just semantics, but Wallpaper Game - Quest RPG might be the thing. If I'm already idling on my phone, figuring out what app to consume, I may as well play around on my wallpaper.

Much like Shaun, I'm going to give Digimon Alysion a try. While I'm nowhere near the level of fan he is, there are a couple of Digimon I've long been a fan of, and I do enjoy card games.

Alongside that, I'm going to give Fishing Inc a whirl. I'm not sure if fishing without the threat of Cthulhu lurking in the deep will appeal to me as much, but you never know until you cast that line.

#4153. GTA 6 Developer Thanks Rockstar for Immortalizing His Late Daughter in the Game

One of the names you can find on a memorial wall in GTA 6 belongs to the daughter of a Rockstar Games developer. Bradley Stone, a lead game tools programmer at Rockstar, has shared the story behind the inscription and thanked the studio for including it in the game. He and his wife lost their daughter Evelyn in 2023, while GTA 6 was still in development.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

Stone shared a video of his visit to the memorial on X on November 27. The video shows Evelyn Stone's name with the date April 8, 2023.

As Dexerto reports, Stone and his wife had experienced several miscarriages before a scan in 2023 revealed that their unborn daughter had a severe case of spina bifida. After further examinations, the couple learned that she wouldn't survive and had to undergo a medical termination five months into the pregnancy.

Stone recalled how difficult it was to leave the hospital without their daughter. He also spoke of his wife's courage throughout the ordeal, which involved nearly a full day of labor. The couple has since welcomed another daughter after going through more difficulties in the years that followed.

Stone thanked Rockstar for giving his family somewhere to remember Evelyn and for supporting him through his grief. He also said the memorial helped “to show this game was made by real people.” He ended his post with a message to his daughter.

“You will forever be in our hearts,” he wrote.

Rockstar hadn't even released the first GTA 6 trailer when Stone and his wife lost Evelyn. That came eight months later, in December 2023. For those of us following the game, the years since then have been spent poring over trailers and wondering when we'd finally get to play it. Reading Stone's account puts that long wait into perspective.

If you'd like to visit the memorial yourself, you'll find it at Deep Roots Memorial Sanctuary, just north of Hamlet. You can also download Rockstar's official Leonida map to help get your bearings if you're unfamiliar with that part of the state. Stone isn't the first Rockstar employee to have shared the significance of one of the inscriptions there since the game came out.

As GAMES.GG reported earlier this week, Rockstar QA developer Matt Green's mother, Beverly, is also commemorated at the sanctuary. He recalled begging her for a copy of GTA Vice City as a kid. She was reluctant at first but eventually agreed, and Green credits that purchase with sparking the interest that led him to a career at Rockstar.

She was proud of his work on GTA 6, but passed away in March this year, before he could show her the finished game. Production designer Terrance Radcliff also lost two family members during development, his father Elhuntry and his first daughter Jade. Their names appear beside one another on the wall. Radcliff shared the tribute on November 22, as the launch week came to a close, explaining how much it meant to him to have both of them commemorated in the game.

What's particularly nice about the sanctuary is that it exists as an actual place within the world rather than a dedication that most of us would miss in the end credits. It's a place that the developers and their families can return to long after they've finished working on the game.

It's a place that the developers and their families can return to long after they've finished working on the game.

From subtle nods to previous games to an Easter egg that lets you revisit the original Vice City, there's plenty for longtime GTA fans to discover in Leonida. The names at Deep Roots carry a much more personal significance, though. I'm glad Stone, Green and Radcliff chose to share their stories with us, and that Rockstar gave them a place to honor their loved ones.

The map of Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive place with many hidden secrets. Have you discovered them all?

#4151. Guide: 43 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' eShop Sale (US)

Every game we scored 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick

Just a reminder that this sale runs until December 2nd, so you've still got plenty of time if you're after a bargain but can't bear the thought of the Black Friday crowds. Carry on!

With Nintendo launching its Black Friday sale on the European eShop earlier this week, we knew it was only a matter of time before our friends in North America got some savings of their own. And what do you know, they have!

Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' sale is now live on the North American storefront, with discounts across a bunch of first- and third-party delights. It'll be sticking around until 2nd December at 11:59pm PT, so you still have a couple of weeks to make the most of it.

Just like with the EU sale, we have assembled the following list of every game in the Adventure Awaits offer that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick from the 8/10s at the end, because we couldn't see it go unmentioned.

As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.

This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.

Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.

Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.

AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

The Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

Difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

Card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre quickly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

Witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.

At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

Plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

This is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

Its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

Along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in said education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

Invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great big colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-new arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole big bunch of new content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the new transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

One of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful new content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Buy Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World

Mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

With a bunch of fantastic new abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great big boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

Give us the Switch 2 Updates for Dread.....AAAAHHHH! xD

Not a bad price for Kirby and the Forgotten Land + Star Crossed World. If you haven't played it yet, this is a very good opportunity to grab a phenomenal game.

How does Slay the Spire only have a user score of 7.5?! What's wrong with you people?! I thought you were cool.

PSA regarding Faeria. I agree that it is outstanding game, and I’ve greatly enjoyed it - even as a solo player. But, last I checked, it still has an always-online requirement. Rather unusual for its genre.

Not a dealbreaker for me personally, but (understandably) a red line for others. Caveat emptor.

I picked up The Talos Principle and The Gardens Between on the cheap this week. The former will scratch my Portal-like itch for the time being.

#4150. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4149. Ironclad: Battle Tank is a top-down tank-busting roguelike coming to Android

What do you do when all hope seems lost, and you're the only one left? Well, clearly you go all out in your tracked war machine and hope to take the enemy down before they do the same to you! And that fast-paced, heavy metal experience is precisely what top-down tank sim Ironclad: Battle Tank promises to provide.

Ironclad: Battle Tank is as straightforward an experience as you can get, and about as subtle about it as, well, a tank. You play as the last lone machine in the fight against the Iron Fleet. Dropped behind enemy lines, each run pits you against bosses in your fight to reach the Citadel and the enormous Dominator that guards it to try and end the war once and for all.

Ironclad: Battle Tank is a refreshingly simple concept for a mobile game, and one that really feels like a throwback to the days of arcade vehicle sims like the Desert Strike series.

Currently in closed alpha, Ironclad: Battle Tank is expected to land on Android sometime in 2027, with no current plans in place for iOS. But watch this space, because if Ironclad turns out to be a rock-solid (metal-solid?) take on the genre, we'll be sure to inform you when it hits iPhone!

If you want something new to play right now, though, then you'll be glad to know our latest list of the five new mobile games to try this week is now live. Featuring some of the most interesting releases from the last seven days that we think are worth checking out!

Deborah Ann Woll, likely best known as Karen Page in Daredevil and Daredevil: Born Again, has just been cast as Laufey in the upcoming live-action God of War series. It's a perfect fit, not just because she's a great actress – Woll already portrays the character in the video games.

The live-action God of War series is currently in production, and after a series of headlines about Kratos, it's refreshing to get some news about his late wife, Faye. Also known as Laufey, she dies right before 2018's God of War (which the show is based on) begins. The game centers on a journey between Kratos and his son to spread Faye's ashes from the highest peak in the realms.

Faye is not present in 2018's God of War, but she appears in God of War Ragnarök in flashback and dream sequences. In this game, she's played by Deborah Ann Woll, an oddly high-profile casting for a relatively minor character. It all made sense earlier this year, however, when we learned Woll will reprise her role as the star of God of War Laufey, which tells Faye's story as she fights through a mythological underworld.

It's a cool piece of news, and it implies that Faye will have more of a presence in the series than in the first game, where she never appears at all. As for what shape that presence takes, we have no idea.

Woll joins the likes of Alastair Duncan, who plays Mimir and will also reprise his role. The two don't really interact in the games, however, so it's unlikely to see them share the screen in the series.

The main news around Prime Video's God of War is about its protagonist. Originally announced as Ryan Hurst, the actor suffered a serious injury on the set of the show and was replaced by Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy, Glass Onion) in August. Other key cast members include Callum Vinson as Atreus, Sonya Walger as Freya, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, and Ed Skrein as Baldur.

#4147. Rockstar Explains Why GTA 6 Is Missing One of the Series' Most Iconic Weapons

GTA 6 has taken us back to Vice City for the first time in two decades, but one of the weapons I most associate with the city hasn't returned. You can find chainsaws in Leonida, but you can't pick them up and use them like you could in GTA Vice City or San Andreas. Rockstar has now explained why.

GTA 6 removes the ability solicit, a GTA feature since 2001. Rockstar says the decision supports Jason and Lucia’s story.

As Dexerto reports, Rockstar felt that the violence associated with the weapon would be too much for GTA 6. It seems the studio is a little more selective about what it lets us get away with now that its games look this good.

In an interview with VGC published on November 26, GTA 6 producer and Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson discussed some of the things that didn't make it into the game. Be warned that the interview contains story spoilers.

When asked about the absence of chainsaws, Nelson said, “I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters.” He then added, “It’s not a resource thing.”

Katanas, another staple of the PS2-era GTA games, are missing from the arsenal as well. It's a little odd to see a chainsaw lying around and not be able to pick it up, especially considering how interactive GTA 6 is compared to its predecessors.

I've always seen the chainsaw as more of a Hollywood and video game weapon than a practical one. In real life, using one against a person would hardly be as straightforward as the movies make it look. The saw could jam, and it would be an absolute mess. I can understand why Rockstar wouldn't want to depict that sort of gore in such detail, given how controversial the GTA series has been over the years.

This is, after all, the same studio that gave us Manhunt. Manhunt 2 even ran into trouble with ratings boards before its release, and I don't think Rockstar is going back to the series anytime soon. It's one thing to make a horror game where the brutality is part of the premise, but quite another to let someone loose with a chainsaw in a modern recreation of Miami.

For me, the chainsaw will always be associated with GTA Vice City. Colonel Cortez gives Tommy Vercetti one in Treacherous Swine, a fairly early mission in the game. It returned in San Andreas, both of the PSP GTA games, and Chinatown Wars. It was already absent from GTA 4 and GTA 5, though, so it's not as if every GTA game needs one.

What I find more interesting about Nelson's answer is his reference to Jason and Lucia. There's a difference between what a protagonist would do in a cutscene and what you can get up to when you're not following the story. Part of the fun of the older GTA games was seeing how far you could stray from the character you were supposed to be playing.

Part of the fun of the older GTA games was seeing how far you could stray from the character you were supposed to be playing.

CJ, for instance, had plenty of reasons to look after Grove Street, but San Andreas never stopped you from abandoning your responsibilities and spending an afternoon flying a jetpack around the desert. Even the weapons you could carry in that game included some pretty ridiculous choices that had little to do with CJ's life as a gang member.

I can live without the chainsaw in GTA 6, especially if the alternative is something closer to Manhunt than the cartoonish violence of Vice City. I'd just hate to see the personalities of the protagonists become a reason to leave out some of the sillier weapons and activities in future GTA games.

From its technical shortcomings to its pacing issues, these are seven details that make GTA 6 a flawed game.

#4145. GTA 6: How to Fast Travel

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

When it comes to open world games, there’s nothing quite as dense as Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar has created one of the most impressive open world games ever, with so much to see and do. It becomes incredibly immersive, to the point where sometimes you want a little more game in the game. One specific feature that is a bit unconventional is the fast travel system, but just how do you do it?

Find Selkie Hole in GTA 6, grab scuba gear, and explore the underwater cave system for meteorites and the Explorer’s Knife.

The obvious question a lot of people might have is “is there fast travel in Grand Theft Auto 6?” This is a massive game with a lot of things to see and do. It’s one of the most densely packed games we’ve ever played, and being an open world, one would expect there to be some sort of fast travel system.

You’ll probably go through a good portion of the game not realizing this, but there is indeed a fast travel system. This is because, even though it’s introduced to you early in the game, it’s something easily overlooked. With that said, it does come with a bit of a caveat to the point, especially early on, it’s not really worth using.

With all of that said, the way you can fast travel is through your phone. First, you will need to put a destination on your map. It can be a custom pin, or it can be a specific location such as a mission marker or clothing store.

Once you have this selected, bring up your phone and select the RydeMe app. This will bring up a standard menu showing how much it will cost to travel that distance you inputed (you can change the destination in this menu) along with ordering a Premium Ryde.

Select the ride and a car will appear shortly. Getting in, though, won’t immediately teleport you to that location. Instead, there will be dialogue, especially if you’re with your partner, and sometimes it is worth it to listen.

With that said, if you want to actually teleport, you can pay the driver an extra $100 to skip the ride and get there immediately. The downside is obviously, early on, this is an expensive way of traveling. Also, it will pass time considerably because the car itself will take a long time to get to the destination without breaking any rules.

Whether or not you want to use the teleport system in GTA 6 will probably be determined how far a place is located, as anything under 4 or 5 miles generally isn’t worth paying for, but when it gets above that, it can be a bit of a stretch – unless you want to take a helicopter or plane.

Learn where to find Vice City International Airport in GTA 6, how to enter by air, road, or fence, and what happens when you steal a plane.

#4144. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4143. Black Panther Actor Says Marvel 1943 One Button Rumor Is “Ridiculous”

Debunking reports that Marvel 1943 had been cancelled, Kotaku claimed on November 11 that Amy Hennig's Black Panther and Captain America-centric game was originally designed for Netflix before transitioning to console and PC, meaning that it's light on gameplay and mostly uses one button. However, Black Panther himself, Khary Payton, claims otherwise.

"I've seen stuff about this game like it's not happening or some people — I think the latest thing is it's a one-button game. I don't know how that could be possible," Payton said in a new interview with Brandon Davis. "I have no idea what that means, but I have literally played the game. I know that's not true. It's ridiculous.

They're going to be blown away by this game.

"This game is so — not just beautiful, people don't understand the level of genius on every level," he continued. "Amy Hennig has put together a team that is phenomenal. And they're going to be blown away by this game. You know what? I look forward to those same guys who say these things on the internet having to eat a little crow. I know that they're going to love it."

While it was reported that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra underwent serious turmoil behind the scenes after transitioning from a narrative-focused Netflix game to a more traditional console title, Kotaku also claimed that production was "close to done," something Khary Payton corroborated. He told Davis that "we have finished the majority" and are now "cleaning up," and while he doesn't have a release date to share at this time, he teased that "it's coming soon."

“I wanted to remind my kid and people like him that they are magic."

With that being said, we know exceedingly little about Marvel 1943. The game is set in occupied Paris during World War 2 and is based on the limited Marvel Comics series Captain America/Black Panther: Flag of Our Fathers, with Howling Commandos' member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali serving as playable characters alongside Steve Rogers and Azzuri (Black Panther), but otherwise, we don't know how it'll play or even what it looks like in its current state. Beyond the initial 2021 reveal, little has been shown.

Hopefully, that will change soon — maybe at The Game Awards (where Iron Man appears to be suiting up for a trailer). Right now, there are a lot of contradictory reports and rumors circulating, and it'd be reassuring to finally have the record set straight.

Paramount want to ensure that Amy Hennig's new team is "Set up for a great future," and that means not rushing Marvel 1943 out the door.

#4141. Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto. Big Walk? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.

It makes it a funny time for The Hero of Time to step back into the fray. After all, the original N64 Ocarina of Time practically set the template for today’s sword-toting successors. Dark Souls, Onimusha, even Kingdom Hearts’ keyblade battles all follow in Link’s Kokiri bootprints.

Ocarina of Time famously defined the lock-on, circle strafing, and the basic choreography of action-game design. According to a 2011 Iwata Asks, that genre-defining 3D swordfighting had a charming origin story (after a fleeting moment where they considered making Ocarina of Time in first-person!). It came about thanks to a ninja show witnessed by co-director Toru Osawa and colleagues on a frankly enviable work excursion to the Toei Kyoto Studio Park.

As Osawa remembered the Japanese period film reenactment, “a number of ninja were surrounding the main samurai, and one lashed out with a kusarigama [a sickle and chain weapon]. The lead samurai caught it with his left arm, the chain stretched tight, and the ninja moved in a circle around him.”

Action choreography was the remaining issue for director Yoshiaki Koizumi. At that same ninja show, he spotted the action movie routine that helps Jackie Chan inexplicably survive every movie:

“First, one attacks while the others wait. When the first guy goes down, the next one steps in and so on [...] Watching that show at the studio park was a clue toward solving that problem. Z-targeting flags one particular opponent, telling the other enemies to wait.”

That impeccable logic meant Link was safe from being mobbed by Keese swooping from offscreen in all directions. It was such a sound design principle that it continues to underpin action games today. But I suspect modern players no longer need to be handled with Koizumi’s kid gloves. Judging by the remake, Nintendo agrees.

Consider how Nintendo changed N64 Ocarina’s Forest Temple’s ominous fight against two Wolfos. Lock on to one, its counterpart scampers obediently into the background. Not so for the remake! These newly terrifying fiends aren’t just tankier, swifter, and more aggressive: they’ll conduct somersaulting tag-team switchups at will so you’re left to deal with a full health bar – just like the Lizalfos duo.

It’s a lesson not every Ocarina successor learned. The latest Onimusha’s greatest flaw comes from how closely its mobs follow the age-old formula. Attacking one at a time, queuing up a procession of theatrical wind-up animations makes them trivially easy for a supremely talented Mushashi to attack, deflect, or even decapitate with a well-timed Issen counter. Dawnwalker’s usually not much better, sending vampire Brencis’s lackeys after you in patient succession.

In comparison, I have to commend Phantom Blade Zero for its willingness to toss out Koizumi’s Law, never passing up an opportunity to give players a well-deserved backstabbing.

But the remake’s multitude of combat changes go far beyond footwork and newly aggressive enemies. For all its modernising under-the-hood changes, playing it still feels like entering a mystical parallel universe where Sekiro never happened. I’m back with sword and shield in hand, without a high-risk, high-reward parry ability.

Even with its snappier, flashier but deeply familiar combat, it took some getting used to a gentler pace compared to more recent upstarts. I started my playthrough thoroughly parrybrained after spending nearly 100 hours playing Dawnwalker into Wolverine before finally catching up with Metroid Dread. When I returned to Hyrule, it was with fingers already twitching with anticipation at every incoming blow.

Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy.

One problem: I was ready to parry but Link wasn’t. In fact, the remake felt close to playing Dark Souls using the almost obligatory sword-and-shield build (with a parry I never learned to use properly!). As our review rightly noted, it’s laudably true to the original game, not even touching The Wind Waker’s combat-geared flourishes like the jump-spin attacks that would follow five years later.

The result is combat that feels almost like a cautious game of chess. You bait a mistake or trigger a weakness before going for the stunlock. Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy. It may no longer be dangerous to go alone, but at least we have a few tips to help up the ante – I just wouldn’t recommend a swordless run!

Along with the absent stamina and posture meters, Ocarina remake’s simpler combat blessedly ignores a more recent swordfighting innovation: light and heavy attacks. Generally, I can live without the added layer of combat timing fussiness the Soulslike dominion has given us. It also avoids the pitfalls introduced by Phantom Blade Zero, where single inputs translate into a continuous flurry of attacks that can feel unsatisfyingly disconnected from the buttons I’ve pressed.

That’s not to say I wouldn’t say no to all modern embellishments. I’d love a high-powered combo finisher such as Wind Waker’s. But don’t forget: Ocarina already had a more entertaining means to deal a slow wind-up finishing blow capable of leaving its victim in a 6ft deep crater. It’s big, it’s bad, it’s the same height as your dad: it’s the Biggoron Sword!

But no matter the size of the sword he wields, Link’s return from the past has the vibe of a strangely youthful veteran checking in on his proteges. Musashi, Coen, and Soul are the new kids on the block, but they learned everything they know from their green-tunicked, rosy-cheeked master.

And if it ever comes down to a showdown, those newcomers simply aren’t getting past Link’s guard when he hasn’t got a stamina meter to wear down.

It would hold up a lot better if it wasn’t so dang easy. Nintendo and their kids’ games… pffft! 🤪

Add to that heavier reliance on magic and item usage during combat, and it would definitely be on par with modern action rpgs.

They need to go back to skyward sword and mix it with Ocarina. Shields have durability, giving you an actual reason to parry well (saving your shield durability meter), other than stunning the enemy with perfect parry of course. And also make the angle with which you swing your sword actually count. Which is something which is absolutely doable with Ocarina's current gameplay, it doesn't even mean motion controls.

And there you go you've got a winner. They have had the right ideas since skyward sword, they just decided to completely ignore them by not even trying with swordfights in breath of the wild. Time to go back to it!

"Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto."

It's a bit bloody difficult to forget when an article that has bugger all to do with GTA, brazenly crowbars it in to the very first line.

Onimusha certainly has more depth and nuance to it's swordplay, which is great, but the simpler style in the Ocarina remake is still fun as hell to play. I love that they really played up the weightiness of Link's strikes. I also loved just how op the Biggoron Sword is. You can pretty much take out an Iron Knuckle with two fully charge spin attacks.

I'd say Twilight Princess still pretty handily has the best Zelda combat.

@Lizuka agreed. I loved learning all the different moves from the zombie hero guy.

It's weird how they made the Ocarina of Time remake's combat so easy compared to both the original and Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom- nobody was asking for it to be so easy.

Also, from a visual feedback standpoint- every slightest sword strike shouldn't be a huge flashy thing like it is in this remake- it feels cool at first, but quickly makes the feedback feel flat- have weaker strikes look less flashy, and just stronger ones or killing blows have that great flashy effect instead- if they're all flashy, none of them are.

The combat in the remake felt like a massive improvement. It's much more satisfying than in the 1998 original. Ruthlessness gets you punished, as it should be.

Still, there are games which have much deeper combat because that's their main focus. Titles like Onimusha: Way of the Sword are clearly superior in that respect.

Dunno if Nintendo would implement an advanced mode or something with future entries, but I would be welcoming it for sure.

@OldManHermit You know the “zombie hero guy” is Link from Ocarina of Time right?

Tp Link is his direct descendant who he chooses to pass his skills down to.

Onimusha might have some of the best swordplay ever. PBZ wins out on making you feel overpowered and flashy but Onimusha really does make you feel like a swordsman. OoT Remake combat is fine and does the job but its no Onimusha or PBZ.

@Mjplaysgames Yes, I've heard that before, it's a really cool detail.

@OldManHermit Cool. I just thought it was funny you called the hero of time a “zombie hero guy”.😅

@Mjplaysgames haha, I should've said zombie hero of time guy.

Quite honestly, Kirby and the Forgotten Land has my favorite 3D swordfighting combat.

Not every game with swords needs combos, parrying , slowmo-triggering dodges, etc. Twilight Princess and Skyward Sword had some interesting swordplay, but the basics of figuring out each enemy's timing and weaknesses are still pretty satisfying on their own.

It more depends on the game you want to make and for what audience. Some folks just want an adventure and to feel like a badarse hero without having to train (part of the reason turn based is still popular). If I want complexity, I put down the controller, pick up the arcade stick and play a fighting game. If I want adventure, usually Zelda is my go to.

Also people are drawn to complexity differently. I will literally train daily in a fighting game learning mix ups and getting a feel for the character, meanwhile capcom can’t pay me to enjoy normal monster hunter (even though I enjoy dragon’s dogma and monhun stories).

If a game doesn’t play like your favorite complex game, that isn’t a negative. It’s simply different gameplay that is designed to evoke a different type of synergy with the player. Sometimes if it ain’t broke really does apply.

#4140. GTA 6: How to Get into the Apocalypse Bunker

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

What’s Grand Theft Auto 6 without a conspiracy theorist character? That’s exactly who Freddie is, a man with his own podcast, and he’s ready for the apocalypse in his big bunker. Unfortunately, you won’t know where to find Freddie as his location is somewhat obscure. There’s nothing to point you in the right direction, but thankfully, that’s why we’re here. We know exactly where to find this bunker, but be warned: it’s not as easy to breach as most hideouts.

Find out how to get into bank vaults in GTA 6, complete Yasmani’s Lombank robbery, escape the police, and get tips on more vaults.

The bunker in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a little trickier to find just because it doesn’t quite point you in the right direction. This isn’t part of a main quest, let alone a side quest, but instead is something that has to be found by exploring.

The bunker in question is located in North Leonard County. This section of the map can be found east of North Kelly County and northwest of Vice City itself. The biggest landmark you can look for on the map is Lake Leonida. The bunker can be found on the northwest road closest to it. You see several dark-colored buildings on the map.

Upon driving up to it, though, you will notice that it is completely fortified with an intercom and an automated message saying automated defenses will end you if you attempt to get in.

Being locked away, there will be the temptation to get in. Thankfully, the first time you do this, it’s relatively easy. If you head to the northeast corner of the bunker’s fence, you will find a water tower with a multi-ladder climb.

Climb up the first ladder and on the small platform, jump over the fence onto the shack below. Congratulations; you have successfully breached the defenses. Unfortunately, it’s not over quite yet. This is because there will be additional defenses set up.

Specifically, there will be landmines spread across the property. The best you can do is go down the road towards the bunker and keep an eye out on the ground. You will hear beeping and a red dot on the mine when you get too close.

When you get close to the bunker, drones will be activated. Simply shoot the two down before they get too close as they will explode and deal a good deal of damage. Afterward, jump down the small slope and walk up to the bunker.

The resident, Freddie, isn’t happy you have got as far as you have, but sees it as a challenge to up his defenses. He will say he will text you when he has installed a better system. Simply wait until he texts you before heading back.

The second time is a little trickier to get in only because he has blocked ladder access to the water tower. Thankfully, he left some excavating tools out in the northwest of the perimeter.

There will be a truck with a large bed, and a bulldozer. Park the truck close to the electric fence and then use the bulldozer’s blade to lift the bed of the truck until it’s slightly above the fence. Jump on the truck and into the bed and then hop over the fence. It’s best to set this up near the water tower to avoid some mines.

Speaking of which, the mines are now a little harder to detect. This is because they’re buried slightly further underground, and you can’t see the red light when you get near them. You will still be able to hear it, but it’s best to use your Focus Mode to see them as they light up.

Moving down the road, avoiding the significantly more placed mines, the drones attack has also been adjusted. He will still send two waves of them, but instead of one at a time, the first wave has two drones and the second has three.

After taking care of them, jump down the slope again and approach the bunker for you to meet Freddie for the first time. Congratulations! You can now enter the bunker and even hang out with the apocalypse-ready Freddie.

#4139. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4138. Grand Theft Auto VI Reaches Highest Concurrent Player Count Ever For PS5, More than 683 Million Hours Logged Already

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and it's already broken so many records that it's hard to keep up. It made $3.79 billion in just 24 hours after its November 19 launch, making it the biggest entertainment launch of all time. It comes as no surprise, then, that Rockstar Games' latest crime saga is also shattering records specifically on PlayStation 5.

In a new PlayStation Blog post, the company has revealed that more than 39 million unique players have booted up GTA VI on PS5, with the game setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer games such as Helldivers II, free-to-play games like Fortnite, and single-player releases like Elden Ring. What's more, PS5 players have already logged a cumulative 683 million hours of GTA VI gameplay – that's nearly 78,000 years' worth of time.

Other records for GTA VI on PS5 include the game giving PlayStation the "largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays," and GTA VI being the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles since the game's launch.

This is likely only the beginning of records GTA VI will continue to break.

In the meantime, read Game Informer's GTA VI review to find out why it's one of the greatest games we've ever played, then read the game's first update patch notes to see what's changed. After that, read Game Informer's exclusive interview with Rockstar about the romance between Jason and Lucia, and then check out this feature on the 102 things we actually got before GTA VI. #4137. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4135. Nioh 3 Comes To Xbox In January, Second Story DLC Launches Next Month

The Nioh series celebrates its 10th anniversary next February, and developer Team Ninja is celebrating with a pair of announcements for its latest entry, Nioh 3. First, the game's second story expansion, Bloody Insurrection, launches next month. Second, the game is coming to Xbox in January, marking the franchise's debut on Microsoft's platform.

Bloody Insurrection is Nioh 3's next story expansion following Hell Rising, which launched in August, and is set to release on December 18. Set in Shimabara in 1638, players will be at the center of a conflict between rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai while encountering familiar faces from previous Nioh games. Returning characters include Tachibana Muneshige from the original Nioh, and Bloody Insurrection will serve as the conclusion of protagonist Takechiyo's story.

Bloody Insurrection also introduces new Martial Arts for each weapon type, new Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals, and a new difficulty mode called Nioh's Journey. This new difficulty option is only available if you've completed the Enlightened One's Journey third playthrough and will allow players to find Ethereal equipment drops that let them acquire the highest rarity items in the game.

Additionally, Bloody Insurrection adds new endgame content called the Battlefield of Carnage. This challenges players with climbing floors, i.e., battlefields, filled with enemies and a boss. Each floor is divided into multiple battlefields, and defeating the floor's boss grants helpful battlefield effects, which can be combined to create unique synergies as you climb higher. Defeating enemies also lets players enhance special equipment "instilled with traces of the Yokai Realm," according to Koei Tecmo, which can only be found in Battlefield of Carnage.

A new edition of the game called Nioh 3: Complete Edition arrives on January 28 and will include the base game and its two story expansions. Complete Edition will arrive on PlayStation 5, PC, and, for the first time, Xbox Series X/S. The base version of Nioh 3 is also coming to Xbox Series X/S on the same date. The original version of Nioh 3 is also on sale at a 50 percent discount on PlayStation and Steam, and the season pass is 25 percent off.

For more on Nioh 3, be sure to read our review, in which we awarded the game a 9 out of 10. You can also check out our interview with Team Ninja discussing the Hell Rising expansion.

#4134. GTA 6: Determining Raul’s Fate

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

The open world Rockstar has created for Grand Theft Auto 6 is massive, but it’s not just about the weird random encounters you will find yourself in. There is a massive, 40+ hour-long story with a whole cast of characters to explore. One of the best characters introduced has to be Raul, a suave thief who Brian introduces to, and one who plays a key component to everything that happens in both chapter 3 and 4.

Unfortunately, like a number of minor characters in the story, there is a scene very late in chapter 4 where his fate seems to be put into your hands. We will go over both scenarios, although you might be a bit disappointed with the outcome.

Spoiler warning for anyone who hasn’t reached past the VCI Takedown mission.

Find Freddie’s apocalypse bunker in GTA 6 and learn how to get inside on both visits while avoiding landmines and drones.

The first option is pretty simple. Raul quickly tells you what happened, specifically, Valentina sold them out and Mendez personally came and tortured him. After that, he tells Lucia and Jason to put him out of his misery.

This is where the “choice” comes into play. This option will initiate a firefight outside the boat, as whoever finds Raul tied up will shoot him in the head. Thankfully, Raul comes ready for anything and has a gun locker in the other room.

Still, doing this yourself is arguably the best thing to do for Raul as he likely would have been killed more horrifically afterward. Still, if you don’t want to pull the trigger yourself, there is another option.

Despite Raul pleading and begging for Jason and Lucia to put an end to his suffering, there is the option to restrain yourself like you can in various other situations thus far. You don’t have to pull the trigger, but unfortunately, Raul’s fate is secured no matter what.

If you decide you can’t put Raul out of his misery yourself, your partner, specifically whoever doesn’t find Raul in the bathroom, will automatically shoot him instead. It’s a pretty anti-climatic conclusion, all things considered, especially considering the shot itself alerts a task force which is converging on the boat.

In the end, Raul must die for the story to continue, and either Jason or Lucia will be the one who pulls the trigger. It’s just a matter of if you, as the player, does it.

#4133. GTA 6's Physical Launch Has Been An Astronomical Success, Despite No Discs

All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.

It turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales. This comes via Christopher Dring at The Game Business, who states that the game enjoyed the largest physical launch since 2019 in the UK, generating £32 million in revenue in just three days.

He goes on to state that GTA 6 is the "No.17 biggest physical game launch in the UK since records began in 1995".

In France, it's estimated that over 1 million physical copies were sold in the first three days, a figure that Dring states is comparable to GTA 5 back in 2013. In Spain, meanwhile, the game achieved the largest physical launch in the chart's history.

It's safe to say then that this has comfortably dwarfed pretty much anything that Nintendo has put out in recent years. Normally of course, we'd be celebrating such success – even if the game isn't actually available on Nintendo systems – but the fact that it's a code-in-a-box release raises a few eyebrows.

With GTA 6 being such a success, Sony will no doubt view this as validation that it made the right decision in ceasing the production of discs from 2028. Other large companies will also likely see it as proof that customers don't care about discs anymore, and will likely lean toward download codes much sooner than Sony's cut-off date.

Nintendo itself, meanwhile, probably won't do anything different – at least for the time being. Stats from recent financial reports indicate that Switch and Switch 2 players still value cartridges, with physical sales still making up close to half of the company's total first-party sales.

Still, it's a troubling result for folks who are still all-in on physical games. It certainly indicates that while there are plenty of folks who begrudge Sony's decision to stop the production of discs, there are many, many more people who just don't give a hoot.

@DennisReynolds Ah, you're accusing those people of lying for clout. Yeah, no. It's been proven you could easily steal codes from the game through just shining a flashlight up to the case, and it's also been proven that copies of the game have shipped without a code at all.

I'm not saying this to "hate" on the game. I've actually recently tried it, and it's fun. Not like "best game ever made 10/10 nothing ever will beat it" fun, but it's still alright. It isn't worth rushing to RockStar's defense and dying on the hill that physical copies of games should no longer be made just because you like GTAVI (or more than likely just because you're allowing a company you like to get away with horrible or shady stuff).

As a whole digital games come with a lot less consumer protection rights. You don't get the ability to own what you buy. If you don't like a game, you can't resell it. If a company false flags or bans your account, you won't be able to have access to your game anymore because they can freely strip away your library at any given time. People have already gone through this with movies that they owned on PlayStation multiple times in the past.

The main reason why physical copies of this particular game are only code-in-a-box releases has to do with how RockStar is trying to both control leaks of the game, while also attempting to control the second-hand market. Something which people took issue with when Microsoft was attempting to do it with the XBOX One years ago- but now that another way was found, people are fine with it. Especially because this game was produced by RockStar, and given RockStar's track record, they're allowed to just abuse the goodwill that they've built and a ton of rabid fans (like you) are willing to defend them for every single thing they do.

The main issue is primarily just that these codes can be easily stolen or that RockStar had manufacturing issues and refuse to give people who spent 80-100 bucks on their game their money back when the case didn't even have a code in it to begin with. I genuinely hope a class action lawsuit happens just so people who ended up paying money for a copy only to not get the game can either get the game they paid for, or so that they can get their money back. If you think it's unreasonable, then I guess you're just going to keep licking that boot until they give you free merch or something.
