Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4131. GTA 6 May Have Upped The Value Of A House That Resembles Jason's

GTA 6 is and will continue to have a huge cultural impact for years to come. What I wasn’t expecting was for the game to seemingly affect house prices. That appears to be what has happened to a home listed for sale in Key Largo, Florida, simply because it kind of looks like the house you start your journey in with Jason.

Complex appears to be the cause of the listing going viral. The account shared side-by-side images of the real house in Key Largo and Jason’s in GTA 6, boldly confirming that the former was the inspiration for the latter.

Realtormoc, a real estate account on Instagram, has also shared information about the property, which is listed on Zillow, with GTA 6 fans having a little fun with it in the replies. Most of them are jokes about Brian, the character who owns the house in the game, trying to make some extra cash from it, while my personal favorite reply is the one that reads, “Hey, I forgot something under the floorboards, I’ll call by at the weekend .”

The house is listed for $739,000, which appears to be quite a bit more than it was worth as recently as a month or two ago. Zillow’s “Zestimate” for the two-bedroom home is $675,000, so the asking price is considerably higher. Those who have played through the first chapter of GTA 6 know damn well that Jason and Lucia weren’t living in a house worth that much, and that’s because despite the viral hype surrounding this real-life house that kind of resembles the one from GTA 6, it isn’t the house that inspired Jason’s starter home at all.

That house has already been discovered by people far more talented than those who saw a blue house in Florida on stilts and connected two very distant dots. Shared by GTABOOM, the house that almost certainly inspired Jason’s much more weathered waterfront home is hundreds of miles away from this one. That’s according to GTA mapping sites that used GTADB to reach that conclusion.

The house that’s more likely to be the one Rockstar used to create Jason’s is far smaller and less looked after, as opposed to the shiny, polished house on stilts you can buy for an inflated $739,000. The potentially real Jason house isn’t for sale, but is estimated to be worth around $257,000, which seems far more fitting for the type of life Jason and Lucia have at the start of the game.

If you were to walk around Key Largo, you would almost certainly see dozens of houses that look like they’ve been ripped right out of GTA 6 because Key Lento, the fictional starting point of the game, is based on that particular part of Florida. It’s only because the $739k house is blue and listed for sale that it has been arbitrarily and falsely dubbed the house that inspired Jason’s in GTA 6.

Using a chainsaw as a weapon in GTA 6 would have been a little too violent.

#4129. Witchbrook Has Officially Gone Gold

The long-awaited cozy magical sim game Witchbrook has officially gone Gold, developer Chucklefish announced today. For those unfamiliar with the term “Gold," it generally means the game is complete and ready to be submitted to platforms for certification (and is less likely to be delayed).

Witchbrook is set to launch on January 28, ending a development cycle that stretches back nearly a decade. First teased in 2017, Witchbrook is a life-sim where players control a witch who begins life in the seaside town of Mossport. This includes making friends, finding love, and, most importantly, enrolling in Witchbrook College to master magic by taking classes and completing assignments.

We're delighted to announce that Witchbrook has GONE GOLD ALL PLATFORMS! 💛 We're can't for you all to join us on the journey on Jan 28th! ✨[image or embed]

Witchbrook is more or less Stardew Valley meets Hogwarts Legacy, as you can also start and run businesses, engage in seasonal events, and interact with fully fleshed-out citizens who have daily routines and schedules to consider. After a development cycle marked by long stretches of silence and several delays, those anticipating Witchbrook can breathe easier knowing the game will more than likely stick to its release date.

When Witchbrook launches on January 28, it will be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.

#4128. Phil Spencer Might Not Be At Xbox Anymore, But He's Still Playing Loads Of Games

Phil Spencer is a legend of the Xbox division, having helped redefine the brand after a disastarous Xbox One launch in 2013, and spearheading such initiatives as Xbox Game Pass, Xbox backwards compatibility, crossplay, and a renewed focus on gaming rather than continuing the push towards "TV, TV, TV" that had proven so controversial.

It's very possible that without his influence, Xbox would have shut its doors over a decade ago.

News Microsoft Considered Pulling The Plug On Xbox Back In 2014

We haven't heard anything from Spencer since he announced his retirement earlier in 2026, but he's still very actively playing games on his Xbox consoles, including some of this year's new releases.

For example, he's racked up 940/1000 gamerscore in Echo Generation 2, 650/1000 in Forza Horizon 6, 585/1000 in Replaced, and he's also been playing the likes of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Gears of War: E-Day, Sopa - Tale of the Stolen Potato, Baldur's Gate 3, Vampire Crawlers and even Sunset Overdrive in recent months.

One of Phil's most beloved qualities as Xbox boss was that he proved himself to be a hardcore gamer, being someone who actively seeks to play games in his spare time. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is somewhat the opposite, admitting back in February that she doesn't "pretend to be the best gamer" and that it's ultimately not her goal to be.

Anyway, Phil is busy enjoying his retirement right now, and we wish him all the best from everyone here at Pure Xbox. We unfortunately never got a chance to meet the man ourselves, but always admired his leadership from afar.

Here's hoping he might start hitting the interview circuit and doing what the likes of Peter Moore and Nintendo's Reggie Fils-Aimé have done in the past, as we'd love to see him sticking around the industry in some capacity going forward.

#4127. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4124. I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too quickly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

If you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The issue is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

When I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a new paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

Romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

What are your favorite video game romances? Let us know in the comments!

#4123. Capcom Is Delisting Exoprimal In A Few Months, Then Killing It In 2027

Can't believe the dinosaurs are going extinct, again!

Capcom has today announced that its dinosaur PvPvE shooter Exoprimal will end service on September 29, 2027, meaning it will no longer be playable after that date. The game is also set to be delisted from digital storefronts, including the Xbox Store, on March 30, 2027.

"We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027."

Exoprimal launched on Xbox Series X|S on July 14, 2023, and suffered a pretty pants opening with only 4,995 players logging in through Steam to play Capcom's new team-based shooter.

Here's a detailed breakdown of what is going to happen to Exoprimal in the months leading to end of service:

Following Capcom's mighty 2026 releases, Resident Evil Requiem and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, I wanted to understand what went wrong for Exoprimal, so I hopped back on. Funnily enough, I was actually enjoying the game, despite it being a ghost town. Only nine players were active at the time, and it really felt like it. It's still a fun title though, which makes the end of service announcement quite sad, at least for me.

#4122. Rockstar Reportedly Shopping Around Red Dead Redemption TV/Movie Rights, But Has Rejected Grand Theft Auto Adaptation Offers

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and yet it's shattering records left and right, following in the footsteps of its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V. Despite that, developer Rockstar Games has reportedly continued to reject Hollywood TV and film adaptation offers for the crime saga series, according to a report from The Ankler. However, the studio is reportedly more open to a TV or film adaptation of its cowboy western series, Red Dead Redemption, according to the same report.

The Ankler reports that Rockstar is looking at possible licensing deals for its long-running western shooter series, which received its last entry in 2018, Red Dead Redemption II, for as much as $100 million. There's heavy emphasis on "possible," though, as there is no confirmation that Rockstar has said yes to any of these offers thus far. It's very likely a TV or film adaptation might never come to fruition – it's common for studios to field offers like this, sometimes with serious intent and other times as a quick look at the ocean of possibilities, as it were.

That said, video game adaptations continue to grow more and more popular, especially compared to their humble beginnings in Super Mario Bros. (1993), DOOM, and Mortal Kombat. Franchises like Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog, CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, renewed Super Mario Bros. and Mortal Kombat efforts, and others, including Street Fighter, Resident Evil, Fallout, and Castlevania, have found great success on streaming services and on silver screens. Given how beloved the narratives of Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption series are, it's not surprising that production studios are interested in adapting those stories for TV and movie theater screens.

In the meantime, players have plenty to experience from Rockstar via its latest release, Grand Theft Auto VI, which launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S last week on November 19. Speaking of that game, read Game Informer's Grand Theft Auto VI review to see why it's one of the greatest games we've ever played, and check out the patch notes for the game's first update.

#4121. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4117. The Witcher 4 Dev Signs New 'Agreements' With Sony, But What Does It Mean For Xbox?

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook"

Michał Nowakowski has also now shared the following tweet about this:

Original Story: Last night, we saw some news starting to do the rounds about The Witcher 4 and its developer CD Projekt Red, with Chief Financial Officer Piotr Nielubowicz stating that the studio has entered into new "agreements" with Sony.

These agreements cover the presence of CDPR games on subscription services such as PlayStation Plus, but also "our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign" - which is the bit we're particularly interested in.

Here's a bit of the transcription via our friends at VGC:

"Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign."

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years."

A lot of people are now speculating that The Witcher 4's "collaboration" with Sony may be akin to what Take-Two has done with GTA 6, pushing the whole "plays best on PS5" campaign and restricting how Xbox is allowed to advertise the game. For example, GTA's launch trailer was solely focused around PS5 for an exclusive window.

It's important to highlight that this is just speculation though, and there may be aspects of these agreements that aren't exclusive at all. We've seen CDPR titles like Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Game Pass in the not too distant past, for example, so the PlayStation Plus agreement doesn't necessarily mean Game Pass is out the window.

Let's wait and see what happens with this, but just keep in mind that we could be looking at a situation where The Witcher 4 gets a bigger push on PlayStation than Xbox when it (hopefully) releases in 2028. We'll also leave you with a fun GTA comparison quote from joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski about the difference between Witcher 3 and 4!

"I’m not going to make a deep dive, full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6, but of course, we did look at the game, we did see the differences... we believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4. It’s been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better-looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game."

News The Witcher 4 Team Talks 'Future Of The Franchise', Confirms 2028 Release Window

They'll be at Gamescom with Witcher 3's new DLC as well

News These Are The 70+ Most Important New Features In The Witcher 3 Remastered

What do you think these agreements mean? Let us know your thoughts in the comments section below.

[source videogameschronicle.com, via videogameschronicle.com]

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

#4116. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4115. Pokemon Anime Delay Could Hint At Late 2027 Winds And Waves Release

A new scheduling gap in the Pokémon anime might give us a clue to the Winds and Waves release date.

Serebii founder Joe Merrick pointed out on Bluesky that for the entirety of his time running the fan site, "there has been a new anime episode each week." However, it was announced today that there will be a nine-month gap between Winter Voyage in December and the new Liko and Roy series in 2027.

"Winds and Waves' obvious schedule changes really messed with things huh," Merrick said. A new series of the show typically launch alongside a new mainline game, so delaying the series to October could be taken as evidence that Winds and Waves will launch later in the year.

Of course, it's also possible the anime's hiatus has nothing to do with Winds and Waves, and that the late schedule is intentional. But it lines up with the Pokémon TCG debacle.

Last month, McDonald's accidentally revealed an upcoming collab for its Happy Meals, with 15 new cards arriving in November 2027 — interestingly, there are no new Pokémon included whatsoever. Not even the Winds and Waves starters.

Pokemon's tenth generation games were just revealed, with Pokemon Winds and Waves launching next year.

The theory goes that the new set will arrive too soon after Winds and Waves to include any new 'mons, which would line up with the anime releasing in October.

Put it all together, and it looks like Winds and Waves will launch in late 2027, narrowing down the release window.

Until we hear from The Pokémon Company, of course, this is all speculation, so it's worth taking with a grain of salt. However, considering that mainline games traditionally launch in November (or, at the earliest, September), it lines up.

If Winds and Waves has been delayed, explaining the wider-than-usual gap in the anime, then maybe it's for the best. Game Freak could certainly use a little more runway with the mainline games.

#4112. Review: Gamesir Nova Vision Controller For Switch 1 & 2 - Unique Features Elevate This Mid-Range Pad

Accessory developer Gamesir doesn’t often make controllers with the Switch 1 and 2 in mind, instead focusing primarily on Xbox and PC. So when it announced the new Nova Vision, my Spider-Sense tingled.

The latest entry in the mid-range Nova line, the Vision adds two unique features: a colour LCD screen for quick and easy customisation, and Hall Effect analogue sticks with adjustable tension without the need for extra tools. At $54.99, this is a compelling controller as it is, but Gamesir has also included a charging stand to ensure you’re always good to go.

The analogue sticks really are the star of the show. Featuring raised, textured edges with a grippy rubber material, they actually share much in common with the PS5 analogue sticks and feel great to use. The Hall Effect technology should keep stick drift at bay, while the transparent domes let you see into the interior – a neat little touch I personally liked. My wife wasn’t keen on it, so your own appreciation may vary.

Adjustable tension isn’t completely new — Gulikit’s TT Pro and Max controllers do the same thing — but this is the first instance I’ve tried a controller that lets you do it without any extra tools. All you need to do is twist the sticks anti-clockwise to loosen the tension, and clockwise to tighten.

At their loosest, the sticks feel light and floaty, good for open-world games like Breath of the Wild in which you need to move great distances. At their tightest, they allow for more precise movements, which might come in handy for racing games like Mario Kart World or first-person shooters like Modern Warfare 4.

Had it required an extra tool to adjust the tension, I might have just left the Nova Vision at one setting and been done with it. However, being able to simply twist the sticks to my desired tension at any point encouraged experimentation based on the game I’m playing. It’s a neat feature, and thankfully they take a fair bit of pressure to twist, so you’re never going to do it accidentally.

The screen acts as your main hub for functions and customisation. You might notice at first glance that the Vision is lacking buttons for Start, Select, and Home - they’re all housed in the screen. Click it on the bottom right for Start, the bottom left for Select, and anywhere near the top for Home.

Then you’ve got the ‘M’ button at the bottom, nestled in between the D-pad and right analogue stick. Hold this down for about five seconds to access the configuration menu. Here, you can select whether to connect to Switch, PC, or mobile, remap buttons to your liking, switch between profiles, adjust motion controls and vibration intensity, and more.

When you’re in the configuration menu, navigation is simple: use the D-pad to highlight menu items, ‘A’ to select, and ‘B’ to go back. When you’re done, just hold down the ‘M’ button again to exit. If you’re wondering where the capture button is, there isn’t one, but a quick double-tap of ‘M’ provides the same functionality. There’s no ‘C’ button for chat, mind you.

Inputs feel pretty good, overall. The D-pad, shoulder buttons, and back buttons are mechanical and provide a nice, satisfying click when pressed. The ABXY inputs, meanwhile, are membrane and considerably quieter by comparison. The main shoulder triggers can be swapped between full motion travel and short, clicky stops, so experiment with this to find your preference.

The back buttons aren’t mapped to anything by default. You can map any individual input to the buttons, or opt for any combo macro up to 12 inputs. They’re positioned nicely, allowing your middle fingers to rest comfortably, and they’re much quieter than some of the competition on the market.

Connection is done in three ways: Bluetooth, 2.4G wireless via a dongle, or a USB-C cable. The 1000mAh battery should comfortably last over 10 hours on a single charge, but if you’re using the included charging dock, you’ll likely never need to worry about this. The dock itself is pretty small and minimal in its design, with a nice, subtle RGB strip that slowly pulses when the controller is docked. And yes, it does feature wake-up support for Switch 2.

Finally, it’s worth mentioning that you can further customise the controller via the Gamesir Connect PC app, allowing you to add your own images and GIFs to the built-in screen. Unfortunately, the downside here is that it’s not compatible with Mac, so I’ve been unable to test this feature out myself.

For the mid-range price, the Nova Vision is an excellent controller for Switch 1 and 2. The built-in screen allows for quick customisation and remapping if needed, while the adjustable tension in the analogue sticks feels intuitive and genuinely useful for different games and genres. Add in Hall Effect technology and the charging dock, and you’re getting a lot of bang for your buck.

The lack of a ‘C’ button is a shame, while introducing Mac compatibility for the Gamesir Connect app would be an easy win. Furthermore, some folks just might not be keen on functions like Start and Home being accessed via the screen. If that’s you, then this probably isn’t for you. For everyone else, the Nova Vision is a solid choice.

The samples used in this review were provided by Gamesir.

#4111. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4110. Hollow Knight: Silksong Free Sea Of Sorrow DLC Releases December 11

Team Cherry promised us an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong's Sea of Sorrow DLC today, and thankfully it was not a tepid one where the studio gave the expansion a loose release window way off in the future. It was a far firmer reveal confirming that the free addition to Silksong will be here far sooner than you might have expected.

The trailer for Sea of Sorrow was part of today's Cherry Time update, giving us a first look at what horrors Hornet will be up against next. That first look at the expansion was coupled with the reveal that it will be available on December 11, 2026, so in just 13 days. The DLC will be free to all Silksong owners, no matter which platform you play on.

There is a lot crammed into what is a relatively short trailer showcasing what Sea of Sorrow has to offer. We're shown Hornet battling new enemies, traversing new areas, and judging by the last thing we're shown right at the end of the trailer, she's learned how to fish. Hornet is shown standing on the shore, casting her thread into the water and immediately getting a bite.

Although Team Cherry promised Silksong would be getting an expansion, Hollow Knight fans were fearful because we've been there before. Silksong itself was originally supposed to be DLC for the original Hollow Knight. However, the project wound up becoming so big that Team Cherry eventually decided it should be its own sequel. I'm sure Hollow Knight fans wouldn't argue with that decision given the benefit of hindsight, but it made the wait for Silksong especially excruciating.

There is no risk that Sea of Sorrow will be held back and used to complete the Hollow Knight trilogy. The expansion's release isn't even getting pushed into 2027. This time in two weeks, we'll all be playing it, and it won't cost you an extra penny to do so. If you own Silksong, you will get the DLC for free on December 11. And if you don't, the base game is still just $19.99 and is about to get a whole lot bigger.

Giving fans roughly two weeks between announcement and release appears to be a cadence that Team Cherry has settled into. There was roughly a two-week gap between the announcement of Silksong's release date and its launch, and that went incredibly well. I can only imagine repeating that pattern for Sea of Sorrow will have a similar effect, and the sequel will get a huge player count spike on December 11, along with a sales spike between now and then as those who missed out at launch play catch up before Sea of Sorrow arrives.

#4109. One Of The Most Successful VR Games Of All Time Is Coming To Xbox In January 2027

Say hello to the flatscreen version of Arizona Sunshine

If you've ever owned any kind of VR headset in your life, you've probably come across a game known as Arizona Sunshine, and we're pleased to say that its new flatscreen version is coming to Xbox Series X and Series S in January!

This is a zombie apocalypse game that served as one of the most successful examples of a proper single-player FPS in the early VR era, first releasing all the way back in 2016. It's obviously received a lot of changes for the Xbox release, most notably in the form of a new third-person perspective rather than sticking with first-person.

Its story focuses around a survivor called "Sunny" and his dog known as "Buddy", the latter of which is now playable in two-player co-op as of this new release. Don't be fooled by Buddy's cuteness though - it's still a gory game and certainly not intended for kids, so just keep that in mind before you hit the purchase button or the trailer up above!

Anyway, Arizona Sunshine was a big deal 10 years ago, so it'll be fascinating to see how well it fares on modern non-VR platforms. The game is already available to pre-order on the Xbox Store at a low price of £21.99 / $24.99, and it also seemingly comes with Xbox Play Anywhere support (meaning you get a free PC copy too).

We'll leave you with more details on Arizona Sunshine below, launching for Xbox on January 21st of 2027.

#4108. Exoprimal, Capcom's Dinosaur Hero Shooter, Will Go Offline And Become Unplayable Next Year

Capcom has been on a truly generational run in recent years, but even their legendary lineup of games was bound to have a few stumbling points. Exoprimal is a prime example – the dinosaur-themed hero shooter was not a terrible game by any means, but it requires online play and hasn't managed to maintain much of a player base. Today, Capcom announced plans to sunset the game, rendering it unplayable by September of next year.

"Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal," an announcement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027." The announcement goes on to specify that the game will "no longer be playable" after that date – Exoprimal is an online-only game which requires an internet connection, so once the servers are offline, that's it.

Between now and September 29, Capcom will bring Exoprimal down in stages. As of yesterday, players can no longer purchase a Survival Pass Premium Tier for seasons 1-4. On March 30, Exoprimal and all its DLC will be de-listed from stores, but software owners can still play it and/or re-download it. Finally, the game will fully shut down by September 29.

Any online-only game has a finite lifespan, but it's still sad to see them go. Many gamers are frustrated in recent years because it feels like they don't really own anything, whether it's a subscription-based product or a digital download that can be discontinued at a moment's notice. It's the primary cause of outrage behind PlayStation's decision to stop producing physical discs in 2028.

As for Exoprimal, our reviewer Marcus Stewart largely enjoyed his time with it, writing, "Exoprimal’s creative subversion of expectations impressed me in more ways than one, and its approach to telling a robust narrative within a multiplayer framework is an example I hope other titles study. I just hope it’s enough to keep the game from going extinct."

#4107. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4106. Grand Theft Auto VI’s Breakout Star is Cool Dog – Here’s How to Meet Them

Grand Theft Auto games are full of NPCs that make the world feel more real, or more alive, or more dangerous. But none of them accomplish what GTAVI’s Cool Dog has done in their small cameo in the game: Be both Cool and a Dog.

What’s that, you say? You’ve been through most of the game at this point and haven’t met anyone named Cool Dog? Well, let’s fix that.

Rockstar seems like it was afraid the player was going to get themselves far out to sea in the ocean, as the fictional Leonida resembles an island more than the real-life analogue of Florida, and not have a way to boat back. It was seemingly so afraid, in fact, that it put together a mechanic to rescue you if you get lost.

To make this happen purposely instead of organically, you must take a boat out into open waters and put yourself as far away from open islands or other boats as possible. I did this by opening fire on my own boat, and after the two or three times it exploded and killed me, I managed to just gently sink one instead. If you are far enough out with no land or ships for miles, you will know within seconds, as you should hear the sound of a jetski and barking around you.

And then you will then meet Cool Dog. If you target them with the dialogue button, their name will show as Cool Dog, and you can question them, and ultimately accept the free ride they are offering you as either Lucia or Jason.

Cool Dog drives the jetski near land every so often, so if you’re just looking to get back, you can hop off wherever and swim the rest of the way. If you let Cool Dog finish their journey, though, they will take you to a little island with a bunch of other still-cool-but-not-as-cool dogs. There, Lucia or Jason can play catch with them, pet the dogs, and get a cool pair of Wraparound Shades themselves from a treasure chest. Playing with the dogs for a while will also get them to dig up treasure for you on the island, which can range anywhere from disposable to useful.

Cool Dog leaves their jetski on the shore, so if you want to leave, you can drive it back. But I like to assume Cool Dog either finds a better one or just picks their jetski up wherever you leave it.

Cool Dog is likely based on Loosy, a Golden Retriever who went viral in May for riding a jet ski around Ft. Lauderdale, Florida. Maybe that’s why the game was delayed, so Rockstar could have time to implement this pivotal feature.

For more on Grand Theft Auto VI, check out our 10/10 review, read about how GTA VI already made more money than any entertainment media ever, our thoughts about why romance works so well in this game,  and our exclusive interview with Rockstar discussing how it executed on that romance so perfectly.

#4105. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4103. GTA 6 Easter Egg Hints Jason And Mandy Have History

Day one, a lot of players were thirsting over Mandy in GTA 6. Jason visits her house shortly before Lucia is let out of prison to fix her sink, and the sleaziest VHS tape tucked away in the attic slowly starts to unfold, as she strips down to a bikini and poses right in front of your handyman. Obviously, nothing happens, but it's not over just because Jason slinks away, even if Mandy's role in the story at this point is practically non-existent.

There's the whole serial killer conspiracy, as players spotted her cleaning blood in her bathroom, sparking some wild theories — like Mandy being responsible for Leonida's string of missing persons. If you try to follow her into the bathroom, she even texts you saying that "if you weren't so hot I'd chop all your fingers off." But what's lesser known is that if you make a trip to a meditation spot as Lucia, there's an interesting flashback that seems to hint that Jason and Mandy have a history.

As reported by IGN, during one of these sequences, you can hear Jason saying, "Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago. You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again."

Jason doesn't mention her by name, but this dialogue seems to come after Lucia was sprung from jail, right around the time the two would've been chilling in the keys by Mandy's house. It'd be a little odd for a flashback to reference an unknown woman the player has no connection to, and knows nothing about. Still, it could be a total stranger, so it's worth taking with a grain of salt, but it would certainly explain Mandy's... obsession.

A Floridian real estate listing has gone viral, but it isn't actually the house that inspired Jason's home in GTA 6.

As Twitter user Lanzino pointed out, towards the end of Act 1, you can sneak up on Mandy while she's talking to a police officer, and she has a few lines that stand out. "I wanted to light his house on fire so many times," she cries. "But I couldn't. I loved him too much! I always thought I had time, you know, to change his mind."

Get close enough and Lucia even calls her a "cray b****." GTA 6 is full of these tiny little mysteries weaved throughout the open world and narrative, and Mandy is a hot-spot for them. If her and Jason really did have history together, and she really is the Leonida Butcher, then maybe it's for the best he broke it off.

The most anticipated video game of all time is a triumph on every level that exceeds years of unbelievable expectations. You're not ready for Leonida.

#4102. Holiday Gift Guide 2026

With the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50

If you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250

For players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The new Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! New entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46

We’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some users with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119

If you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99

The question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50

While the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25

Many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s important that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99

The original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the company has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but currently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059

Many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200

Kyle Hilliard contributed to this article.

#4100. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.
