#4084. The Big List Of Upcoming Video Game Remakes

Remakes tend to be more exciting than remasters because the improvements often go beyond mere bumps in resolution or framerate. At best, studios reimagine classic experiences in exciting new ways, sand away rough edges, and somehow retain the intangible x-factors that made fans fall in love with these titles in the first place. At the very least, remakes offer a great way to play antiquated or less accessible experiences on modern hardware.

The remake boom has been in full swing in recent years to the point that it’s starting to get tough to keep track of all the projects in the works. Thankfully, we’ve gathered as many of the announced remakes (not remasters or reboots) that we could find and gathered them in one neat list, arranged chronologically by release window. This will be an evolving list that will be updated as new remakes are announced and released, so be sure to keep an eye on it over the coming months.

Rayman Legends Retold is an exciting yet somewhat controversial remake. The 2013 platformer is arguably Rayman's finest outing, and much of that praise stems from its fantastic and timeless 2D illustrated art. Retold maintains the spirit and perspective of that aesthetic but renders it in 3D courtesy of Ubisoft's Snowdrop Engine. While Retold still looks great in 2.5D, it's debatable whether it looks better than before, but at least the actual gameplay still looks top-notch. New music levels bolster old favorites (such as the iconic "Black Betty" stage), plus additional tracks by Grant Kirkhope, and other quality-of-life improvements should make for a big return for one of the best platformers of the 2010s.

This remake of 2012's Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair retains the game's original zany story but adds a brand-new scenario for fans to sink their teeth into. The game's cast of classmates returns to endure a mysterious new murder game promised to be as substantial as the existing campaign, which itself has been upgraded with visual enhancements. Monokuma has never been better, and that's likely bad news for his unwilling participants.

Record rebuilds Fate/Extra, the first entry in the dungeon-crawling RPG series, with updated character graphics, and a beefier narrative. In terms of gameplay, developer Type-Moon Studio states it features “a more strategic deck-building style of dramatic command battle.” We’re not sure exactly what that last bit means, but given that the original game was released for PSP, it will be nice to have an improved version of the cult title on modern hardware.

After giving Romancing SaGa 2 the remake treatment in 2024, Romancing SaGa 3 is getting a similar glow-up. That means full 3D graphics, voice acting, new musical arrangements by original composer Kenji Ito, and refined gameplay. Square Enix has quietly done a good job reintroducing Romancing SaGa to existing fans while bringing newcomers on board, and it's cool to see them apply the same love and care they've shown Final Fantasy VII over the years.

Lara Croft's 1996 debut adventure has been remade before, but Legacy of Atlantis will be its biggest overhaul yet. Built using Unreal Engine 5 (and, controversially, AI tools), Legacy of Atlantis will feature modernized gameplay as well as a few surprises to Lara's trek across Peru, Egypt, Greece, and the titular lost city. If developers Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog add anything that can top the sheer shock of seeing a T-Rex for the first time in the original game (which returns in its full glory in this revamp), we'll be extra impressed.

Persona 5 may be the entry that dominated the mainstream, but the also critically acclaimed Persona 4 set the table and is getting another shot in the limelight. Unfortunately, we don't know how Atlus plans to update the 2008 title; its 2025 reveal trailer announced it as being in early development. Persona 3 Reload is likely the best reference point for what to expect, and we're looking forward to spending dozens of hours hanging with the gang (i.e., fighting demons) in Inaba one more time.

The final chapter of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy is at hand, and it looks like Square Enix is going out with a bang. Players can now more quickly explore the vast world aboard the Highwind airship, allowing them to then skydive to their destinations. With Cid and Vincent fully playable, the party is complete, and the already stellar combat has been bolstered by a new FITS system, which allows the cast to don new outfits that bestow class-like abilities (FFX-2 dress spheres are (kind of) back, baby!). In a welcome change of pace, Revelations will launch on all platforms simultaneously, meaning no one has to wait to see how Cloud and Co.'s remixed adventure concludes.

Despite only releasing in 2022, Gungrave G.O.R.E. is getting a remake called Blood Heat. Rebuilt entirely in Unreal Engine 5, Blood Heat serves as a redemption of sorts for the poorly received action game by bolstering it with a host of improvements. Upgrades include a revamped and more polished combat system, enhanced cinematics, 360-degree controls, improved enemy AI, and new characters. Here's hoping Gungrave's comeback sticks the landing this time.

11 Bit Studios is reimagining its 2018 post-apocalyptic city-management game, moving it into Unreal Engine 5 but offering more than a visual overhaul. Frostpunk 1886 will boast new content, including an entirely new Purpose path and new mechanics and laws. It may seem a bit soon for a remake of Frostpunk, but the game will be nine years old by the time 1886 is scheduled to launch in 2027.

This remake of the 2002 sim strategy game Europa 1400: The Guild bolsters the original's appealing premise of operating a business within a complex simulation of medieval life with better visuals and new gameplay features. Whether alone or with friends in multiplayer, you'll form a dynasty by starting a family, climbing the social ranks, managing a business, and navigating a web of political intrigue by creating alliances or rivalries with others.

1999's Heroes of Might & Magic III was one of the most beloved strategy games of its time, and Ubisoft is rebuilding the game in full 3D with 4K resolution. The remake is more than a visual upgrade; it also boasts improved animations and audio, a unified campaign with new cinematic cutscenes, a prologue and epilogue, and it includes the two expansion packs: Armageddon's Blade and The Shadow of Death.

Professor Layton's inaugural adventure was a standout title for the Nintendo DS, and this remake brings it to consoles for the first time. The character portraits have been replaced with fully 3D models, and the presentation has been converted to a widescreen, higher-resolution format – a big upgrade from the blurrier visuals of the DS version. Unfortunately, as much as we love the original game, our excitement for the Curious Village remake is dulled by developer Level-5 confirming it is using generative AI in the game's development.

Resident Evil fans hoped and prayed, and Capcom finally answered by announcing its next remake is the beloved (and challenging) Code: Veronica. Like the previous Resident Evil remakes, Claire Redfield's 2000 survival horror adventure has been treated to a major graphical and gameplay overhaul. Although the reimagined storyline will be largely faithful to the original, expect to experience new narrative elements as well.

Santa Monica Studio is going back to its roots by remaking the original God of War Trilogy. Details were non-existent at the game's reveal in February 2026,  but this would presumably be a graphical and potentially gameplay overhaul of Kratos' Greek adventures in God of War, God of War II, and God of War III. Whether this will be a bundled collection of three remade games or if Santa Monica somehow combines them into one seamless experience remains to be seen.

In April, Remedy Entertainment pleasantly surprised the gaming world when it announced it had struck a deal with Rockstar Games to remake Max Payne and Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne. Remedy sold the IP to Rockstar in 2002, but the two are partnering to revive the gritty crime series that popularized Bullet Time. The project, which will combine both games into a single title, will be made by Remedy with Rockstar footing the bill on development and publishing. It's slated for current-gen consoles and PC.

Presentable Liberty, released in 2014, was a 1-to 2-hour-long narrative adventure in which players controlled an imprisoned character during a pandemic. While in solitude, you receive letters over the course of five days that, while you can't reply to them, gradually tell the game's overarching story. Presentable Liberty's original creator, Robert "Wertpol" Brock, had planned to remake his games but passed away in 2018; this upcoming remake is being made in tribute to his life. It will feature more worldbuilding, improved graphics, new items and interactions, new endings, and full controller support.

Bloober Team surprised many by knocking its remake of Silent Hill 2 out of the park. Following that game's positive reception, it's no surprise Konami is entrusting the team to give the same treatment to the 1999 original that first instilled the fear of fog into players. We're excited to see how Bloober Team reinvents Harry Mason's captivating and terrifying search for his missing daughter.

It might not be a new entry, but a remake of Sam Fisher’s first outing is better than nothing after years of waiting. Ubisoft Toronto sits at the helm of the project and plans to rebuild the game from scratch using the Snowdrop Engine while maintaining the classic stealth elements. Here's hoping it can recapture and reinvigorate the stealth gameplay that put the franchise on the map over two decades ago.

The reveal that arguably the best Star Wars game ever was getting a much-needed remake had fans raising their lightsabers in celebration. Unfortunately, the game’s development seemingly succumbed to the dark side after reports surfaced that progress had stalled, and work on the game has switched hands from Aspyr Media to Saber Interactive. The game went radio silent for a long period until Embracer Group sold off Saber, prompting the studio's CEO to confirm that KOTOR is "alive and well".  In March 2026, Saber reconfirmed that the project is still in development. We hope that's the case and look forward to eventually seeing the remake in action.

CD Projekt Red’s litany of upcoming projects includes a full remake of the first Witcher game. It’s being built in Unreal Engine 5 by developer Fool’s Theory with supervision from CD Projekt veterans. The Witcher, released for PC in 2007, is not an easy game to revisit due to its age and lack of console ports. Now that Geralt and friends are mainstream draws, newer fans can finally experience the adventure that started it all.

Team Meat describes this remake of its 2010 indie classic as "everything you remember from Super Meat Boy presented through the wonderful lens of nostalgia with stuff added to it." The skin-tight platforming remains intact but now boasts new art, music (by original composer Danny B), cutscenes, secrets, and more. Team Meat says it wants to make fans feel like they're playing Super Meat Boy for the first time again with this remake (hence the name), and with new secrets to uncover, it's a tantalizing excuse to revisit one of the best platformers ever made.

Although marred by the same generative AI concerns as the Professor Layton remake, this definitive remake of Yo-Kai Watch 2: Bony Spirits/Fleshy Souls/Psychic Specters will likely be exciting for franchise fans. Haunted Domain will feature new story content, better graphics, and new missions, but specific details are under wraps for now.

Which remakes are you looking forward to playing the most? Let us know in the comments!

#4083. Square Enix Says Its Efforts Supporting Switch 2 Have Contributed To Its Strong Financial Results

It's one of the platform's biggest third-party supporters

Square Enix has been one of the biggest third-party supporters of the Nintendo Switch 2, and it seems it's already paying off.

In the Japanese company's latest financial report, Square Enix president Takashi Kiryu has credited year-over-year net sales (¥11.6 billion to ¥35.6 billion) and operating income (¥8.0 billion to ¥13.0 billion) profits partly to its sales on Switch 2. Here's what he had to say:

Takashi Kiryu: "Efforts such as supporting new hardware, including the Nintendo Switch 2, and strengthening catalog title sales also contributed to our results. In the second half, in addition to FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, which launched on October 22, we plan to release DRAGON QUEST MONSTERS: The Withered World in December and Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United in February 2027. All are new titles, including remakes."

As touched on here by the president, Square Enix most recently released Final Fantasy Resonance on the Switch 2 and this will be followed by Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World in December and Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United early next year.

This follows its release of games such as Dragon Quest VII: Reimagined, Kingdom Hearts Collection, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth and more this year. It's also released its MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV Online on Nintendo's hybrid platform in August, and next April sees the arrival of Final Fantasy VII Revelation.

#4082. Poll: Are You Still Happy To Pay For Online Multiplayer On Xbox Consoles?

I'm not sure paid multiplayer makes sense anymore

Paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.

Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.

Xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly. Just a few months ago, I bought Subnautica 2 to play with a friend through the Xbox PC app. I could've opted for Steam, but I wanted to work towards those Xbox cheevos (when they eventually arrive). For a couple of weeks, I'd hop on the PC and dive into alien waters with my mate.

One day, I fancied playing on the big screen in my living room, so I installed Subnautica 2 on my Xbox Series X, booted it up and was prompted to buy a Game Pass subscription just to play the same save file I'd been enjoying for weeks through the Xbox PC app. Like I said, a bit silly.

Time went on, and I'd more or less let this go from my head until I read a report from Windows Central a couple days ago, claiming that Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix next-gen console could have plans to kill paywalls for paid multiplayer.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer."

According to Jez Corden, the original plan for Xbox Helix was to create a console-PC hybrid with access to Steam, potentially spelling the end of Xbox's staple multiplayer charges. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. If you can play your Xbox games across both console and PC, whether through disc-to-digital or Xbox Play Anywhere, it seems like pointless friction to lock multiplayer behind a paywall depending on which device you're playing on.

Back in 2021, changes to Xbox's paid multiplayer requirements allowed players without an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to access multiplayer free-to-play titles such as Fortnite, Call of Duty: Warzone and Apex Legends. And today, Xbox Live Gold isn't even a thing, as it's been absorbed into Xbox Game Pass.

So, even if Xbox Helix's original vision has changed somewhat from what Corden initially reported, it's still not out of the question to suggest that paid multiplayer could eventually become redundant.

Pure Xbox, we'd love to hear what you think about this. Make sure to vote in the poll below and tell us more in the comments section.

Report Major Details Revealed About Xbox's Original Plan For Project Helix

#4081. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4080. Jupiter's Picross Series For Switch Has Officially Surpassed One Million Sales

The first title released on the eShop in 2017

If you've ever bought one of Jupiter Corporation's Picross games on the Switch, you've helped the series reach a major milestone.

The Kyoto-based developer has this week announced its Picross series for Switch has now surpassed one million downloads. Since the launch of Picross S on the Switch in 2017, Jupiter has gone on to release more than 20 Picross titles (including all sorts of crossovers).

Earlier this year in March, we saw the release of the Picross S Konami Antiques Edition, which featured popular Konami IP such as Castlevania and Contra. The news of one million sales this week happens to be taking place ahead of the release of the new game Picross S Climax.

Picross S Climax launches on the Japanese eShop on 10th December 2026. To help build some excitement, Jupiter has released a demo for the new title. There'll also be a series sale taking place on 30th November 2026, with the Konami Antiques Edition going on sale for the first time and Picross S 50% off.

Jupiter's history with the Picross video games stretches way back to the Super Nintendo and Game Boy era, with titles such as Mario's Super Picross and Mario's Picross. These games can now be accessed via the Switch Online 'Nintendo Classics' service.

#4079. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4078. GTA 6 Appears To Be Causing Issues On A Small Number Of Xbox (& PS5) Consoles

FWIW, it seems to be happening more on PS5

Over the last few days, I've been running into various bits of discussion on social media about how GTA 6 is crashing or even "frying" some people's consoles, and for the most part it's been talked about in regards to the PS5 version.

This particular clip has been getting a ton of attention this week (profanity warning):

The Verge editor Tom Warren ended up picking up on this, suggesting that "GTA 6 is really stress testing the GPUs inside consoles", and then pointing out that the Xbox Support Reddit community highlights issues on Xbox as well.

And after visiting it, yeah... there's no doubt it's got multiple reports from people who claim GTA 6 has been responsible for either crashing their console or putting stress on the GPU and causing the visuals to stop functioning properly.

Here are just a few examples of people confirming their issues:

Now, as scary as this might seem, it's worth keeping in mind that you're unlikely to run into any major issues. The majority of GTA 6 players are enjoying the game just fine on their Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S and PS5 consoles right now, and I'm willing to bet most people haven't had a single crash whatsoever.

It also should be noted that Rockstar aimed to reduce crashes in their latest update for GTA 6 this week.

News GTA 6 Update Now Live On Xbox Series X|S, Includes Seven Official Fixes

Update: We've got the deets from Rockstar

At the same time, it's also impossible to say how widespread the problem is, but most people speculate that it's limited to anywhere between 0.1% and 5% of Xbox players at most. GTA 6 is an incredibly demanding game without a doubt, and it might unfortunately be exposing some weaknesses in certain consoles for whatever reason.

That's why we're only saying "a small number of" consoles in the headline here, because we don't want you to get scared off from playing GTA 6 over the next few weeks and months. Just keep in mind that it's a good idea to ensure your console isn't too clogged up with dust every now and again, and hopefully you'll never run into issues like this.

Feature Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

News GTA 6 Comparison Reveals Two Advantages Of Xbox Series X Over PS5

#4077. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

#4076. PS5's Most Overlooked Action Game of 2026 Gets a Complete Edition Next Year

Nioh 3 is getting a 'Complete Edition' early next year, Koei Tecmo has confirmed. It'll include the base adventure alongside its two expansions, Hell Rising and Bloody Insurrection.

The latter isn't actually out yet — it launches on the 17th December, and promises a brutal all-out battle between multiple factions. Your character will, naturally, be tasked with carving out a solution to the bloodshed.

Anyway, I think this Complete Edition — set to release on the 28th January — is worth highlighting because it really does feel like Nioh 3 got left behind this year.

Team Ninja's sequel received super strong reviews and it was fairly popular at launch, but it's fallen off a cliff in terms of recognition. That's largely because it launched so early on the 6th February, which has meant that it's been buried over the course of 2026.

In particular, the success of other, much more recent action games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Phantom Blade Zero has prevented it from even being brought up in most conversations.

Case in point: Nioh 3 hasn't received a single nomination at The Game Awards. It's nowhere to be seen under Best Action Game, Best Action / Adventure Game, or Best RPG.

Just anecdotally, I've seen a handful of Push Square users expressing their love for Nioh 3 in various comments sections; it's clearly got fans, but it feels like the game needs a miracle if it's to show up in any end-of-year discussions.

Have you played Nioh 3, or did you miss out? Might you be eyeing up this Complete Edition? Equip some better gear in the comments section below.

#4075. Pokémon Champions X Pokémon GO Collab Taking Place Next Month

As you've likely already seen, Pokémon Champions is getting a balance update, more Pokémon and more Mega Evolutions next month on 2nd December 2026.

A week after this, there'll also be an in-game collab taking place with the mobile hit Pokémon GO. This campaign takes place between 8th December 2026 and 18th December 2026, and during this time, you'll be able to unlock a Professor Willow Outfit Set and 10 Training Tickets.

"You can obtain the Professor Willow Outfit Set one time only by bringing Pokémon you befriended in Pokémon GO to Pokémon Champions as visitors.

"You can obtain the Training Tickets by bringing Pokémon you befriended in Pokémon GO to Pokémon Champions as visitors. You will get one Training Ticket the first time you bring a Pokémon first discovered in each of the regions"

These rewards can be obtained in the Switch and mobile versions of Champions. These rewards may also be made available in the shop (or other areas of the game) at a later date.

During the Pokémon Champions Celebration Event in Pokémon GO (between 8th December 2026 and 14th December 2026), you can expect encounters with Charmander, Starly, Grookey "and more" in the wild. You'll also have the chance to encounter Absol, Gible, and others. You can find out more details about the Raids, Event Bonuses, Field Research (and more) on the Pokémon GO website.

"Each of these Pokémon is especially valuable on Pokémon Champions teams once they’ve been fully evolved (except Absol, of course, who’s ready for action right away). There will also be an increased chance to encounter Kecleon at PokéStops!"

You can find out more about the upcoming update for Pokémon Champions in our previous stories:

Update: Studio confirms lack of Xbox version

Update [Fri 27th Nov 2026, 3:38pm]: Developer Playtonic has now confirmed we won't be getting an Xbox version (at least at launch). We've shared their statement elsewhere on Pure Xbox:

News Yooka-Laylee Developer Issues Statement On Why Definitive Edition Is Skipping Xbox

"...just isn't viable for us at this time"

Original Story: Here's a strange one for you! The fantastic Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair has been one of the best platformers on Xbox since it launched back in 2019, but the game's new "Definitive Edition" appears to be skipping Series X and S.

A new announcement today revealed that the upgraded Definitive Edition will include enhanced visuals, up to 4K resolution at 120FPS, two orchestrated soundtracks and more, but it will only be available on PC, Switch 2 and PS5.

As you can imagine, that hasn't gone down well with Xbox fans.

The comments section of Playtonic Games' post is full of reactions like these, and at the time of writing, no response or statement has been provided for why the Definitive Edition isn't coming to Xbox in addition to other platforms.

There may well be a very good reason for it, and here's hoping we might get clarification at some point in the near future, but at least for the time being, it seems we're going to have to miss out on this new enhanced version.

As disappointing as this is, the 2019 original is still well worth playing if you're interested!

#4073. Quote of the Day by Stranger Than Heaven director: "Age and career length are not deciding factors"

Mikinobu Abe says RGG Studio lets younger devs' creativity speak for itself

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In any job, experience can be crucial. The ability to make decisions based on years or decades of insider knowledge is a valuable skill. But when your industry changes as fast as the games industry does, relying exclusively on your most longtanding employees isn't always a recipe for staying at the cutting edge. That's why Mikinobu Abe, game director of Stranger Than Heaven, the new historical offering from Yakuza/Like a Dragon developer RGG Studio, says that it's not all about experience.

Speaking to Edge magazine as part of a massive Stranger Than Heaven profile, Abe says that his background as a fluent English speaker gave him a "helpful perspective" on the game's story. Focusing on Daito, a half-Japanese, half-American character who has returned to Japan after growing up in the states, Stranger Than Heaven offers a different approach to the studio's other offerings. Abe suggests it's not his language skills that helped him secure the director role, but instead studio head Masayoshi Yokoyama's philosophy around creativity.

"We have a philosophy that age and career length are not deciding factors," Abe explains. "We make decisions based on each person's ability and creative sensibility." As for his own role at the forefront of the studio's next game, he says it was neither his age or his background that got him the director position: "I personally feel it wasn't about simply giving the younger generation an opportunity, but because the project needed to be something truly new."

That novelty already seems to be on display. Stranger Than Heaven looks to borrow some of that Like a Dragon DNA, but it also appears a far grittier, more down-to-earth outing, with some of that linked to its historical setting, taking the audience back in time, away from the neon-soaked streets of modern Japan all the way to the 1910s, working slowly forward through the 20th century. There are plenty of RGG Studio veterans who might have been excellently-placed to make another game in the series that made the team their name, but perhaps it was felt that their experience would limit Stranger Than Heaven's ability to feel like an entirely new experience.

We've got plenty more where this came from, thanks to Edge Magazine's expansive cover feature on Stranger Than Heaven, which features hands-on impressions, as well as input from Abe, Yokoyama, and more of the RGG team. It's available in full, for free, right here on GamesRadar+, exclusively for members.

#4072. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4071. Final Fantasy Resonance Devs Surprised by How Many Fans Wanted a Traditional, Turn-Based RPG

Final Fantasy Resonance has been one of the most positively-received Square Enix games in ages — but its developers were never fully convinced that it would, er, resonate on the scale that it has.

Producer Keisuke Nakashima told Japanese outlet Game*Spark (as translated by Automaton): "I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of FF they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art."

Of course, this quote feeds into a debate that's been raging amongst fans of Final Fantasy for over a couple of decades at this point.

There are many who believe that the series has long since lost its way, pushing to innovate with more and more action-focused gameplay instead of drawing from the turn-based and command battle systems that helped establish the franchise as a world-beater in the first place.

Titles like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 are constantly brought up as living proof that turn-based RPGs can still be blockbusters — but Square Enix has only veered further and further away from Final Fantasy's traditional blueprint with each mainline instalment.

Resonance may be a lower-budget spin-off, but at least to some extent, it does go against the publisher's line of thinking that Final Fantasy must appeal to a "wider audience" if it's to maintain its flagship status.

"We figured [Resonance] was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way," says Nakashima.

Director Hiroto Furuya adds: "I thought this was a rather unconventional title, so I expected opinions on it might be divided."

He then references Resonance's foundations, having been built on the bones of now defunct mobile title Final Fantasy Brave Exvius: "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it."

Without wanting to be overly critical of games I really enjoy, like Final Fantasy 16, I do think Square Enix has been guilty of chasing a goal that simply may not exist.

This mythical "wider audience" has been the downfall of many games over the years, and you can argue that Final Fantasy has chipped away at its own identity and strength of brand in the (pretty desperate) pursuit of new fans.

Resonance isn't going to sell millions upon millions of copies, but the way it's been embraced says a lot about the current state of Final Fantasy as a whole, I feel.

And remember, recent reports strongly suggested that the suits at Square Enix wanted Resonance to be a basic port of the aforementioned mobile title, presumably in a bid to keep costs down.

Are you glad Final Fantasy Resonance exists? Do you think Square Enix needs to learn from its success? Take a turn in the comments section below.

#4070. Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.

This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.

On this page: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

If you want brief directions and as few spoilers as possible in terms of item unlocks and progression, then use the following abridged walkthrough to take you through the game. If you want extra specifics - including useful optional extras as you go - then check the following section.

For a more detailed walkthrough of the critical path, this section can explain specific steps on how to progress. If you want even more detailed step-by-step guides to the game's many dungeons, then follow the links to dedicated pages on each.

Before you can visit the Great Deku Tree, you must find a Sword and Shield, otherwise Mido won’t let you through. You can find the Kokiri Sword in the Forest Training Center to the southwest (crawl through the vent to get there, then find it in the chest above), and the Deku Shield from the shop in the northeast by collecting Rupees found scattered around the village.

Visit the Deku Tree, complete the Great Deku Tree dungeon, and get the Kokiri’s Emerald key item and an instruction to head to Hyrule Castle. Now leave Kokiri Forest to the west to receive an Ocarina in a cutscene before leaving to Hyrule Field.

Head directly north along the path until you reach the castle drawbridge. The area inside is the Hyrule Castle Market - there’s lots of optional activities here, including the chance to get your first Bottle from the Potion Shop - and when ready, proceed to Hyrule Castle, where after getting the Weird Egg from Maron, you must make your way through the grounds to meet Zelda.

You'll now have Zelda’s Letter and learnt Zelda’s Lullaby on the Ocarina. The critical path is to Death Mountain via Kakariko Village, though you should visit the Lost Woods first (for Saria's Song, which you'll need shortly) and ideally, an optional visit to Lon Lon Ranch (for a Bottle and the first step in how to get Epona).

When ready, go east from Hyrule Field’s drawbridge and up the steps to Kakariko Village.

After finding all Cucco locations for a Bottle and visiting the Graveyard for the Sun’s Song (both optional), show Zelda’s Letter to the guard at the north exit. He gives you an optional errand - returning to the Hyrule Castle Market for a "proper shield" (the Hylian Shield) and also to start the Happy Mask Shop quest.

Guide All Great Fairy Fountain Locations In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Powerful upgrades for a small fee? Fairy 'nough

The aim is to reach Goron City. Hug the rightmost wall: this will take you up and round the corner, then back on yourself up the cliff. The path will now split: take the left branch to Goron City.

Inside Goron City, head to the lowest level, where on the north side is a closed door. Play Zelda’s Lullaby here to open it. Inside is Darunia. Talk to him, then play Saria’s Song (which you can get from the Lost Woods). This will see you unlock the Goron’s Bracelet, allowing you to use Bomb Flowers.

Now leave Goron City the way you came (the top entrance), then go directly right to see a Bomb Flower near a fence. Now you have the Goron's Bracelet, throw it over and you’ll bomb the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, allowing you to enter.

Once you have completed the Dodongo Cavern dungeon and picked Bombs and the Goron’s Ruby (the Spiritual Stone of Fire), feel free to scale Death Mountain for a Great Fairy Fountain location (unlocking Din's Fire) before heading off to Zora Domain.

Zora River - which leads to Zora Domain - is just east of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain on Hyrule Field.

Reach the end - the way there is fairly linear - and access Zora Domain by playing Zelda's Lullaby at the waterfall.

Inside, you must find the whereabouts of Princess Ruto by getting the Silver Scale in a mini-game at the top of the waterfall, then by visiting Lake Hylia via the underwater shortcut for a Bottle with a letter inside. (Our dedicated Zora Domain walkthrough features more specific directions for all these, by the way!)

Speak to King Zora, Bottle up a fish found in Zora Domain, then give it to the giant fish in Zora Fountain to access Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly dungeon.

Once the dungeon is complete and the Spiritual Stone of Water is in your possession, head to Hyrule Castle. After the cutscene, dive in the moat and collect the Ocarina of Time, where you’ll then learn the Song of Time.

Head to the Temple of Time which branches off from Hyrule Castle Market. Inside, stand in front of the inscription at the far end, and play the Song of Time. Now go into the next room and retrieve the Master Sword.

After the cutscene, you’ll become Adult Link, and are told to head to Kakariko Village. Do so, then head to the Graveyard. On the left row of graves is a tombstone with flowers in front; push the stone and head down the hole. Now follow Dampe through the maze and at the end, you’ll receive the Hookshot.

To leave, play the Song of Time on the blocks, to emerge in the Windmill. Use this opportunity to get the Heart Piece opposite, then speak to the man to learn the Song of Storms - you’ll need this later.

With the Hookshot in hand, you can explore more of Hyrule, but when ready, head to Forest Temple: it can be found at the end of the Lost Woods, and inside the dungeon, you'll unlock the Bow and be rewarded with the Forest Medallion story item.

Complete the Forest Temple dungeon to unlock a Sage. At this point onward, upon returning to the Temple of Time, you can time travel back into Young Link by putting the Master Sword the pedestal. Also, to help, Sheik will teach you The Prelude of Light, which allows you to teleport back to the Temple of Time - a pretty handy shortcut.

As Adult Link, make your way to Death Mountain (it’s worth going into the Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village now you have the Bow, which rewards you the Big Quiver to hold 40 Rupees as you go), then head into Goron City.

On the next level down is a Goron rolling around, and your aim is to detonate a Bomb near him so he stops. Once successful, the Goron will reveal their name is Link, son of Darunia, and will explain the Goron's plight.

Exhaust the dialogue options to receive the Goron Tunic - a red garb which allows you to withstand high temperatures - and directions to the Fire Temple, which is by heading to Darunia’s room (located on the bottom level at the back) and then by pulling the statue to reveal a route to the Death Mountain Crater.

Once in, go over the drawbridge using the Hookshot to meet Sheik, who will teach you Bolero of Fire. Now head through the left doorway, drop down and follow the passage to reach the dungeon, unlocking the Megaton Hammer and the Fire Medallion along the way.

Before you leave, it's worth going south across the bridge from the exit to Goron City in the Death Mountain Crater and using your Megaton Hammer on the cave entrance to get the Magic Meter upgrade from the Great Fairy Fountain within.

Head to the Ice Cavern, which is located in Zora Domain (or specifically, in Zora Fountain where you encountered Lord Jabu-Jabu as a child). Doing so will see you unlock the Iron Boots; make sure you grab a Blue Fire before leaving, and return to Zora Domain and use the Blue Fire on King Zora to free him and receive a Zora Tunic, which allows you to breathe underwater for an unlimited amount of time.

With both the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic in hand, we have everything we need to take on the Water Temple. Play the Serenade of Water to be teleported there when ready. Completing this will see you receive the Longshot - a Hookshot upgrade - and the Water Medallion.

Before we move onto the next temple, on this island is a plaque in front of you which hints at a puzzle involving the morning sun. If you are reading this as soon as the Water Temple has wrapped, the sun should still be rising: aim for the halo with your Bow and fire an Arrow, which will see it transform into a Fire Arrow on the platform ahead.

(As an aside, provided you have completed the previous three Adult Link temples, and have unlocked Epona, you now have everything you need to take on the optional Biggoron Sword trading sequence quest.)

Guide Biggoron Sword Trading Sequence Quest In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

When you’re ready, head to Kakariko Village as Adult Link. When you arrive, a cutscene plays showing the place on fire, Sheik appearing, and a spirit emerges from the well. You’re then taught the Nocturne of Shadow, allowing you to travel to the Shadow Temple - though there’s a place to visit you need to visit first - the Kakariko well.

As it's currently blocked off as an adult, you need to return as a child. If you haven’t already, learn Song of Storms from the Guru-Guru inside the windmill, then return to the windmill as Young Link and play Song of Storms back to him (now you have the Nocturne of Shadow, the return journey will be a lot quicker).

Doing so will cause the windmill to spin out of control and lower the water in the well. Drop down and complete the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon to get the Lenses of Truth.

Guide How To Get The Lenses Of Truth In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

If you haven’t already, you also need Din’s Fire. This is acquired by visiting the Great Fairy Fountain location at the top of Death Mountain. Now you have Din’s Fire and the Lenses of Truth, play Nocturne of Shadow, then use Din’s Fire in the centre of the torches to gain access to the Shadow Temple, where you’ll get the Hover Boots along the way, and another Medallion.

With that done, it’s time to head to Gerudo Valley. It’s found in the west of Hyrule Field, and you need either the Longshot or Epona to make it over the bridge at the start.

Complete the Gerudo Fortress stealth section - essentially let yourself get captured, then find the four carpenters so you can explore freely - then past the Mirage Desert trials (you need the Longshot and the Lenses of Truth) to reach the Evil Desert Colossus area and the Spirit Temple.

This unlocks two new items - the Silver Gauntlets and the Mirror Shield - and another Medallion.

There are two optional extras in this region - a Great Fairy Fountain in Evil Desert Colossus (Nayru's Love; Bomb the cracked wall on the north side) and within Gerudo’s Fortress, the Gerudo Training Grounds (a mini-dungeon which grants the Ice Arrow).

Assuming you have now awakened every Sage and received every Medallion, it’s now time to head to the Temple of Time and start the final stretch of the game.

A cutscene will play and you’ll receive the Light Arrow, and an instruction to head to Ganon’s Castle.

Approach the lava moat around the castle to form a bridge with the help of the Sages. Now enter.

The Inside Ganondorf's Castle dungeon within is composed of six routes from a central hub, each with a 'Barrier' you must destroy; though you can tackle them in broadly any order, go for the Shadow Barrier first to get the Golden Gauntlets, which is required before tackling certain other routes in the dungeon.

Once that - and a brief trip to the Great Fairy Fountain just outside the castle beyond the bridge for a useful defensive upgrade - it’s time to scale the tower, or to halt your progress so you can mop up any remaining side-quests and collectables (see the end of this guide for a list) before the finale.

The tower within Ganondorf’s Castle is essentially a short gauntlet of battles until you reach Ganon himself at the top, and from there, it’s a linear stretch until the end credits. Good luck!

Here is a list of side quests, items and collectables you can find.

#4069. 10+ Xbox Games Are Releasing Today, Including A Dangerous Twist On Mario Party (November 26)

"New twists on the party genre for sessions of fun, screaming, and horror"

December is just around the corner, yet we've still got plenty of November games to get through.

Today's lot might not look like much, but there are a few interesting games worth keeping tabs on, starting with Machine Party. Launching with Xbox Play Anywhere support, this dark and dangerous Mario Party-inspired title pits you against your friends in a series of murder-themed mini-games.

Also launching today is Security 51, another XPA title that's giving all sorts of Papers, Please vibes. If you don't know what I'm talking about, the game essentially has you working as a security guard, checking documents and questioning visitors to Area 51. Not everything is as it seems though, so keep your eyes peeled, yeah?

And finally, there's The Spectrum Retreat: Redux, a first-person puzzler from an award-winning game dev. Personally, I don't know much about this one, but on the surface, it looks pretty cool.

So, here's what's new on Xbox today (November 26):

On this page: 10+ Xbox Games Are Releasing Today, Including A Dangerous Twist On Mario Party (November 26)

In this series of dangerous, and some would say highly illegal, party games you will have to use every trick in the book to survive. Play through classic party game formats and new twists on the genre for sessions of fun, screaming, and horror.

Security 51 is an atmospheric security guard simulator inspired by Papers, Please, and SCP paranoia. You’re on duty in the underground bunker of Area 51, where the most dangerous part begins at the elevator: the shaft descends for miles down to unknown levels.

The Spectrum Retreat: Redux is a first-person puzzle thriller created by Dan Smith, Winner of the 2016 BAFTA Young Game Designer Award.

#4068. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#4067. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4066. Random: Did Dave The Diver Just Tease A GTA 6 Collab? It Seems Unlikely, But Some Fans Are Hopeful

If you didn't already know, Dave The Diver actually has something in common with Rockstar's new open-world title, Grand Theft Auto 6. In both games, you can go diving!

Now, can you imagine a collab? Well, before we get too carried away, GTA 6 might already be on the mind of the Dave the Diver developer Mintrocket, as the game's official social media account has shared a rather amusing image today. Here it is:

If you've been playing GTA 6 over the past week, this character may look familiar, as it appears to be Mintrocket's nod to an individual known as Brian (not to be mistaken with the Dave the Diver character, Cobra). The male protagonist in GTA 6 (Jason) works for Brian.

The whole look, including the shirt, seems very similar to Rockstar's character. And then there's the Vice City-like backdrop. Just about every reply to the post so far seems to be open to the idea of Brian coming to Blue Hole in some way or form. However, as one fan notes, it might be hard to get him out of retirement.

While there's no guarantee anything will come of this, it's worth noting Dave the Diver has already done some crazy (and high-profile) crossovers with titles and series such as Yakuza: Like A Dragon and Godzilla. Dave has also appeared in games such as Epic's battle royale, Fortnite.

As part of the GTA 6 marketing campaign, Rockstar did a collab with NBA 2K27, another title under parent company Take-Two.

#4064. PS Plus Essential Games for December 2026 Announced

These games will be available to claim until 4th January, 2027 after they’ve been added to the sub next week.

It’s the final update of 2026 and PS Plus Essential is going out with a bit of a bang in my opinion.

Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 is the most recent remake in Activision’s long-running skateboarding series, and a very good compilation at that.

We awarded it an 8/10 in our review, writing: “Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4 is another fantastic skateboarding title that revives some all-time classics, albeit with some caveats.”

Meanwhile, Dragon Ball XenoVerse 2 is arriving just ahead of its sequel next year. This game has received years of support, including a fairly recent PS5 port, included here as part of your subscription.

Of that PS5 version, we wrote in our 7/10 review: “The only problem with XenoVerse 2, here in 2024, is that its core gameplay has never truly evolved. Yes, more and more ways to upgrade and customise your character have been added over the years, but the actual combat feels basic and a touch too finicky by today's standards.”

Finally, Amnesia: The Bunker is an acclaimed horror game from specialists Frictional – and one we ultimately liked.

We said in our 7/10 review: “Amnesia: The Bunker sticks a little too close to what Frictional Games has been doing for over a decade now, but with a more free-form approach to gameplay, the team is back on the right track again.”

That rounds out the lineup for December, then – and 2026 as a whole? How are you feeling about PS Plus Essential this year? Let me know below.

#4063. The best Lego Black Friday deals 2026, found by experts

Lego Black Friday deals have officially arrived, and they're bringing some major discounts in their wake. No matter whether you're trying to track down playsets for your kids or a display piece for your shelf, there's a discount with your name on it.

Actually, you can save up to 40% right now; the sale has been pretty generous across a range of themes and interests. With that in mind, it's well worth checking out regardless of whether you're just browsing, you've got something specific in mind, or you want to find a gift for a Lego-obsessed loved one. In my experience, you're unlikely to get a better opportunity all year; I've spent most of a decade writing about the best Lego sets for GamesRadar+ and can't think of a sale that provides more value for money than the Lego Black Friday deals.

Because there's a lot to choose from, our team of experts and I are busy rounding up as many bargains as we can. These aren't just decent offers; they're the best savings we can find, checked against price history and other trends. You'll also find plenty of advice here, all based on the many years I've spent covering Black Friday Lego deals.

Benjamin has written about Lego at GamesRadar+ for almost eight years, but he's adored the toy since he was first able to click those bricks together as a kid in the 1990s. He's usually got multiple projects on the go at once, and right now he's finishing Lego Minas Tirith alongside the haunted Mayor Manor.

Of all the Lego figures to drop in 2026, this is one of the best - we had a good time with it in our Lego Shrek, Donkey, & Puss in Boots review. The set has never been cheaper than it is now, and considering it only came out a few months ago, that's noteworthy.

Seeing as this kit is an exclusive to the Lego store, came out very recently, and hasn't ever had a discount before, I'd say this is one of the better Lego Black Friday deals so far. OK, so the design is a bit marmite - but if you want a festive addition to your Christmas display or you need for a gift for someone who adores Elf, there's no denying how good this price cut is.

If you ever need an easy gift, I always recommend Lego's Botanicals range. Besides looking downright beautiful, they're a quirky, interactive present so should delight the recipient even if they don't have any other experience with Lego to speak of. This offer provides a three-for-one combo that's never been cheaper than it is now.

Of all the Pokemon sets to drop in 2026, this might have been one of the most anticipated. Opening up like a Polly Pocket-style clamshell that's like my childhood come to life, it reveals Professor Oak's lab and a trainer battle pulled straight from the original Pokemon Red and Blue video games. That gives it a really nostalgic feel, which is potent when mixed with a record low price. We've never seen it for less than this.

Is that a record low price I can see? As the droids would put it, "roger roger." Based on the Trade Federation Battle Droids from Phantom Menace, this kit is a striking celebration of the Star Wars prequels that rarely drops below $120.

I know it's a board game rather than a set, but wait - this one is an official Lego board game. It features a crew of Ninjago ninjas working to defeat foes on the Destiny's Bounty ship, and it got a lot of attention when I saw it at board game conventions earlier this year. It's now $29.99 at Amazon, reduced from $40.

Now that we're starting to come to the end of Black Friday, I'd really recommend jumping on any offers you've had your eye on - there's no guarantee they'll stick around for long, because people typically wait until the last moment to snap up offers. As such, leaving it too late means you may end up with an 'out of stock' notice before you can hit checkout.

Time to set sail! The Going Merry ship from One Piece is currently in port with a record low price, both at Amazon and Lego itself. This is arguably one of the most iconic locations in the entire series, so it getting such a steep discount for today's Lego Black Friday deals is good news if you want to add a bit of bountiful One Piece merch to your collection.

Is it worth becoming a Lego Insider to take advantage of the official Lego store Black Friday deals? Honestly, yes - it costs you nothing, is minimal effort, and boils down to being the site's sign-in with some perks. As such, I'd definitely grab an account if you don't have one already and were considering getting some of today's offers.

Want a cute Lego table decoration to make Christmas feel just a bit cozier? This candle and wreath design is now 40% less at Amazon, making it a whole lot more affordable (it's now just $23.99). I think this is one of those more subtle but incredibly effective display pieces that you may not instantly realize is Lego, but should put a smile on the face of anyone who looks closer.

You can then throw in the Gingerbread AT-AT Walker at $48.65 at Amazon to complete the trio.

Want to grab something from the latest Spider-Man movie? This Brand New Day-inspired truck chase kit is still sitting at a record low price during 2026's Lego Black Friday deals, which is $39.99 via Amazon if you were interested. Something I've not looked into too much are Lego lighting systems. These are specifically made for individual sets and basically make them come alive when the night draws in; windows glow, engines flare, and lanterns flicker. Plenty of them are on sale for this year's Lego Black Friday deals at Amazon, so it's worth checking to see if your favorite set has a bespoke lighting system to jazz it up (it almost certainly does).

While it's not a deal, I think it's worth pointing out that Lego Godzilla officially launches today on Black Friday. (Phew, what a release date.) It's exclusive to the Lego store so you won't find it anywhere else, but it does come with a free gift-with-purchase if you're quick. That's a wrecked city skyline behind the Godzilla logo, in front of which is a huge, ominous footprint belonging to a certain kaiju.

And that's me back in the saddle! I'm Benj, and I'm taking the reigns of this Lego Black Friday deals guide again. Have you managed to pick up anything in the sale? Sound off in the comments section below, and let me know if there's anything specific you're trying to track down.

I've been tracking Lego Black Friday deals for several days now, and one retailer has been performing way above and beyond the others - Amazon. Yes, I know it's a "well, duh" kind of answer considering how massive the store is, but it genuinely has had the best variety of Lego sets and the most tempting price cuts. I'd prioritize it as a result.

Before we properly kick things off, here are couple of pointers to help you discern discount gold from disappointment. I use these tips when tracking down discounts myself, and they've served me well since I started tracking sales in 2018.

💲Use price comparison software: This is probably the most helpful bit of advice I can give, and it applies to everything on sale - not just Lego. In short, I'd highly recommend using price comparison software like CamelCamelCamel. This allows you to check an item's full price history, providing info on record lows and average costs. That means you can find out whether a price cut is actually good or not. Not all savings are created equal, you see; sometimes they're distinctly average.

⭐ Make sure there's a 'Black Friday deal' badge: There are countless offers filling the digital shelves, but I'd be hesitant to grab anything that doesn't have an official 'Black Friday deal' badge attached (unless it's a record low price, anyway). If it's got one of those, you should be safe from it being discounted further as we move through the weekend.

#4062. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4059. Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair Gets a PS5 Definitive Edition, Out This December

Playtonic has announced Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair is being treated to a new Definitive Edition on PS5, and it's right around the corner.

The new version launches on 15th December 2026, and anyone who owns a digital PS4 version of the game gets a free upgrade. It appears anyone with a physical copy won't get the upgrade.

On base PS5 and PS5 Pro, the new edition will support a 4K resolution at 120fps, better lighting and ambient occlusion effects, higher-fidelity shadows, and two orchestrated soundtracks. Also, if you don't already own it, the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack is automatically bundled in with the PS5 version.

One of the best platforming adventures of its generation is back, enhanced for PlayStation 5. Yooka & Laylee return for a full-scale 2.5D adventure, with a 3D Overworld that's an adventure in its own right, levels you can alter to create new ways to play, and Capital B's Impossible Lair waiting to test your skills.

A 2D and top-down side game that accompanies the main Yooka-Laylee game, the Impossible Lair went down really well upon its original launch. It's got an 82 rating on Metacritic, and in our own review, we called it an "improvement" on the original adventure.

#4058. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.
