"You'd be nuts to take on all of that in the first project, and yet here we are"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Witcher 3 and Assassin's Creed raised the bar for modern RPGs during the development of Fable, says Playground Games co-founder Ralph Fulton, so the team had to rise to the challenge.

Over six years after its 2020 announcement, we're almost there, with Fable set to release in February 2027. But what took so long? Speaking to GamesIndustry.biz, Fulton starts, "it's a new team, it's a new genre, a new franchise, [and] new technology."

And that's not all; he also points to Fable's humor, quest structure, combat, and simulations as things that need to be mastered. "You'd be nuts to take on all of that in the first project, and yet here we are," he says.

Another challenge is that "technology has advanced" over the course of development and new games are constantly raising the bar.

"The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard," Filton says, "and after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG."

Those hits are something the team took notice of, with Fulton explaining they "continue to reset player expectations." He adds, "I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects."

Fable has been pretty dormant for some time. Not counting the ill-received Xbox Live Arcade and Kinect spinoffs, the series hasn't had an actual release since 2010's Fable 3 (and even that isn't as loved as the original two titles).

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Playground Games' reboot has similarly been in the works for some time, with rumors that the developer was leading it emerging in 2018 before it was eventually revealed two years later. Come next year, we'll finally see if it'll be worth the wait.

#4056. Xbox Console Sales Get A Huge Boost In The UK, While GTA 6 Breaks Records For Physical Games

Series X and S sales received their biggest jump since 2024

We've got some new data coming out about the UK games market in November 2026 today, and unsurprisingly, it's a market that's been absolutely dominated by the launch of GTA 6 last week.

According to the folks at The Game Business, sales of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S rose by a whopping 75% during GTA 6's launch week, which represents the biggest jump for Xbox hardware since 2024.

The PS5 was close behind at 46%, and console sales were up 38% overall (after a 29% increase the week before).

In terms of UK console sales, PS5 sales rose 46% during the week GTA 6 came out, while Xbox Series S and X sales jumped 75%. It’s the biggest jump for Xbox since 2024. Overall, UK console sales last week were up 38%, which comes on the back of a 29% increase the week prior.

Meanwhile, the controversial "physical" edition of GTA 6 broke numerous records in Europe, serving as the biggest physical launch in Spain's history according to their charts, and selling over 1m physical copies in France in three days.

It was also the biggest physical launch in the UK since FIFA 20 in September 2019, and is the 17th biggest physical launch since records began there in 1995. This is according to data provided by UK data tracker Nielsen IQ.

"GTA 6 is the biggest physical game launch since 2019, reveals UK data tracker Nielsen IQ. It generated £32 million in revenue in just three days."

Just last week, on the day of GTA 6's release, we mentioned how Xbox hardware spending in the U.S. was up 42% YoY in October, attributed to the likes of Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6.

It's going to be fascinating to see how the rest of the world stacks up in terms of Xbox sales data from November (which should be revealed over the coming days and weeks), and indeed whether GTA 6's physical edition is also setting records in even more regions. It most likely is - this is a ridiculously popular game after all.

#4055. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4054. Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC News and 'Exciting' Reveals from Dev Team Cherry Coming This Week

Team Cherry will provide an update on the Sea of Sorrow expansion it has in the works for Hollow Knight: Silksong this week, alongside a selection of other "exciting announcements".

A timed YouTube presentation is already uploaded to the developer's channel, with the description: "Join us for Cherry Time! A special presentation with a bunch of exciting announcements, and an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow!"

Having released last year, Team Cherry has shared Hollow Knight: Silksong will be treated to multiple content updates, and Sea of Sorrow is just the first. It's been slated to launch in 2026 for a while now, so it seems likely we will get a firm release date on Friday, 27th November, when the video airs.

As for the other reveals, I wouldn't get your hopes up for anything substantial like another game or a look at the next big DLC. I would expect these updates to be more like merchandise lines and physical collectibles for fans.

Still, it's nice to know we'll learn about Sea of Sorrow at the end of this week.

#4053. Doug Bowser 'Apologises' To The "Haters" Of His Icky AI-Generated Thanksgiving Post

Happy belated Thanksgiving to all of our friends across the pond! As you all wake up to tummies full of turkey, you'll be pleased to see that former Nintendo of America President Doug Bowser has wished everybody a good one, too. The only difference is, he did it with a grim AI-generated post.

Oh, brother. Bowser shared the image yesterday, showing him sitting behind a Thanksgiving spread with Bowser and Donkey Kong posing next to him.

Only, that's not Bowser and DK, but an AI rendition of the pair. Bowser's cloak doesn't make sense, his crown defies the laws of physics, there's a mushed-up hand on Doug's shoulder, and the less said about DK's tie, the better. C'mon, man.

Bowser wasn't quite tone deaf enough to keep the image up for long, taking it down after receiving several comments expressing their disappointment that the former NoA President (who, we're sure, has a plethora of human-edited pictures of him and Bowser/DK at his disposal) would stoop to sharing something like this.

Oh hey Doug Bowser made a Thanksgiving po- Oh…

But Bowser just couldn't let it lie. After deleting the post, he shared the following message on X, 'apologising' to the "haters" of the image:

Apologies if I offended people with my AI generated post. It was sent to me by a friend and it made me smile. For the haters out there the message remains the same - I wish you a Happy Thanksgiving.

Ugh. A genuine apology would have been fine, Doug. In fact, just deleting the post and sharing something human-made instead would have sufficed. Throwing in a little "haters" line pushes the whole thing to another level of out-of-touch.

You'll be pleased to hear that there were no AI posts from the current NoA President, Devon Pritchard. Hey, as a palate cleanser, here's the post that Nintendo of America shared on its socials to mark Thanksgiving. Rest assured, it's far more wholesome.

Feature Who Is Devon Pritchard? - Meet The Next NOA President Stepping Into Bowser's Boots

#4052. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#4051. Analyst Suggests Console Prices Won't Drop Until At Least 2028

"If data centre demand grows, then it could quickly eat into the extra supply"

We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too. But if you were hoping 2027 would be the year things finally get cheaper, well, according to S&P boffins, it doesn't look likely.

Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching new consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.

According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".

"[2028 is] the earliest point at which launching new consoles at accessible price points looks prudent,"

In layman's terms, these digits suggest supply might finally begin catching up with demand in 2028, potentially bringing down the cost of PCs and consoles.

DRAM is essentially a console or PC's super-fast short-term memory. Whenever you boot a game, its data is loaded into DRAM so it can be accessed and processed quickly. The more DRAM you have, the bigger and more ambitious games you can play.

The image above gives us a breakdown of the additional DRAM supply expected from each manufacturer, pointing to 2028 as the earliest point at which prices could start to get smaller.

However, that's relying on a consistent demand from data centres. If it continues to grow, all that additional DRAM could be gobbled up by the AI industry. Likewise, if demand is less popular than predicted, supplies could return quicker.

"If data centre demand grows, then it could quickly eat into the extra supply...The memory [fabrication facilities] are not expanding with an eye specifically toward the consumer market. They're racking up record revenue and margins on the data centre build-out, so these supply expansions are primarily meant to feed that demand."

Microsoft's next-gen Xbox Helix console is rumoured to be launching in 2028 with a suspected price tag of over $1,000. Barbour weighed in on Microsoft's Xbox Series supply shortages.

"If Microsoft is suffering from supply shortages with the current Series consoles, as it has said a few times over the past year, then they will almost have to wait for the upstream component supply to shore up before they make a big push with a new console."

Report Major Details Revealed About Xbox's Original Plan For Project Helix

We've compiled the ultimate list for what you can stream this weekend, including new movies arriving on streaming, original releases, and the finale to one of our favorite shows.

Blade Runner 2099 tells a new story set in the beloved franchise, some 50 years on from when we last entered the neon-streaked sci-fi world. It's a very different setting this time around too as replicants have now taken power following an uprising. In this harsh landscape, Cora (played by Hunter Schafer) forms an unlikely pairing with a dying replicant called Olwen (Michelle Yeoh).

Across the eight-part drama, the pair try to track down a runaway who is harboring a truth that could collapse their fragile city. Reviews have been pretty positive for this one with plenty of praise for the impressive worldbuilding. All eight episodes are out now as well, making the perfect binge-watch for this holiday weekend. As well as charting their lives and their experiences on the battlefield, the film focuses on the iconic football game that was played before the Battle of Okinawa, a fascinating part of military history. #4049. Rare Co-Founder Tim Stamper Unveils A Treasure Trove Of Conker Dev Material

Rare co-founder Tim Stamper has begun uploading new videos to his YouTube channel 'InTimsWorld', the first of which being a deep dive into the development of Conker's Bad Fur Day (thanks, Time Extension).

Released in 2001, mere months before the GameCube landed, Conker's Bad Fur Day is one of the most recognisable titles on the N64, garnering critical acclaim and controversy in equal measure thanks to its raunchy themes and platforming satire.

Stamper's video is mostly a peek into a folder containing a wealth of artwork and design documents from the game's development. It's a really fascinating glimpse into how the game evolved into the final product, with Stamper also providing the odd anecdote here and there.

Tim Stamper, along with his brother Chris, left Rare in 2007, a few years after the company was bought out by Microsoft. Rare's output in recent years has been pretty slim compared to its earlier days, with Sea of Thieves being the most significant success story.

With Xbox implementing major restructures to its business, Rare now reports directly to Activision, which Microsoft previously purchased for almost $69 billion.

#4048. Guide: GTA 6: Secret Controls the Game Doesn't Tell You

GTA 6 has a complicated control scheme that allows you to interact with the game in a variety of different ways. And while Rockstar does a good job introducing almost all of the title's mechanics, several useful features and commands are never mentioned at all. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you about some of its secret controls.

On this page: Best Secret Controls GTA 6 Doesn't Tell You

Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.

Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.

Double tap Triangle to get out of your car while the engine's still running:

This can be useful for when you need to make a swift getaway, as you want waste time needing to start the engine.

One other quick tip here: if you're with a partner and need to quickly get into the back seat, hold Triangle so your character doesn't waste time running around to the passenger side.

If the police know your identity but not necessarily your car, one way you can avoid being detected is by hiding behind the wheel.

Just park up somewhere discreet, and hold Circle to hide from any pursuing police:

You can rest and lean on any surface by standing close to it and holding the Circle button, like shown:

This can be useful if you're casing a joint, or just want to watch the world pass you by.

You don't always need words to get your point across. There are situations where a middle finger will do.

Fortunately, GTA 6 has a solution for scenarios just like that.

While on foot, hold L2 and press R1 to give someone the finger:

You can also do this while driving by simply pressing R1 while behind the wheel:

Tapping Left and Right while driving will turn on your indicators, allowing you to signal to other motorists which way you're going:

This can actually be useful when you're trying to drive safely, as oncoming cars will understand which way you're going and react accordingly. It can also help when you're merging lanes on motorways.

While more complex radio controls can be accessed by holding Left, did you know you can also quickly turn the radio on and off by double-tapping Left?

This works both in a car and when you're out and about using your earbuds.

If you press Square while driving, you can quickly attack with your car door, as shown:

This is really useful when you're being flanked by unsuspecting bikers — or you just want to show cyclists who's king the road!

Much like the above car door attack, you can kick any nearby enemies by pushing Square while you're riding a bike, as shown:

This can help you knock rival motorcylists off their bike, or just give you a good core workout while on the highway.

You can go first-person at any time while you're on-foot and stationary by holding L2 and pressing R3:

You can move the camera around from this position and press R2 to zoom, but you do need to hold L2 down throughout.

It's also worth noting you can't move while doing this, as there's no traditional first-person mode in the game.

This can be useful for reading signs and other looking closely at other objects in the game, though.

Every vehicle has a full suite of options you can access by holding Left and using the right analogue stick to navigate up to Vehicle, as shown:

These options can include everything from winding down your windows to turning on your headlights. Speaking of which, you can also toggle your headlights at any time by pressing Circle:

And, if you're in a boat, you can use the above vehicle management options to set down an anchor, which will keep it in place while you go diving:

If you're playing on the PS5, the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers will help you observe the speed limit.

While you're driving, holding R2 until you feel the first point of resistance. This is the speed limit.

You'll need to have Adaptive Triggers Resistance enabled to feel this, and you can check it's on by pressing Options > Settings > Controller > DualSense Wireless Controller Features:

You can take two cars when you're with your partner by using the command menu.

Hold Right to bring up the menu and press Cross/X to instruct your partner to drive:

Then get in another car and hold Right again then press Square to follow you:

You'll notice that your partner will drive right behind you, which can be useful if you need to setup getaway cars during robberies:

Did you know about any or all of these secret controls in GTA 6? You can find even more tips and tricks through the link, as well as tons of collectible and mission walkthroughs in our GTA 6 guide.

PlayStation Buttons based on work by VictorPines, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

#4047. Xbox CSO Responds To Criticism Around Game Branding, Promises To Fix In 2027

"We are fixing this. Will roll out in 2027."

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are announced and Xbox doesn't make a big deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

In other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and new Fallout games where it felt like they were announced without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is announced / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

Let's see what happens in the New Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

#4046. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

GTA 6 was subject to more than a few leaks in the run-up to its eventual launch, but despite it all, one big early-game twist was kept a total secret until release – something Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson was "praying" for.

Before we get into it, we're obviously about to discuss some spoilers for GTA 6 Chapter 1. It's an early moment – one you'll have seen if you've played the first hour of the game – but if you're yet to dive in, you might want to bookmark this to come back to later. Or, of course, feel free to carry on if you don't care about a spoiler-free experience.

Everyone still here who wants to be? Great. As you probably guessed, the twist in question is the existence of Jason and Lucia's son, Tomás.

After being moved to her aunt's care following her arrest, as shown in the game's prologue, Lucia's primary motivation is to get Tomás back and give him a good life alongside Jason, but none of this was revealed prior to launch – officially or otherwise. This was something that co-studio head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, had his "fingers crossed" for.

In an interview with VGC a few days before GTA 6's launch, Nelson confirmed that Rockstar was "never" planning to reveal the twist and, at the time, was still praying no one would spill the beans ahead of schedule. "I am still holding on," he said. "Fingers crossed, how many more days? I'm praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we've gone through, every day I'm just like, 'please, please don't do that, please don't do that.'"

While VGC notes that there was a small amount of chatter on forums about Jason and Lucia having a son, these whispers generally didn't stick, and, notably, none of the Cyberleek videos that appeared online before launch showed Tomás. Honestly, that feels somewhat miraculous given how early he's revealed and how frequently he comes up in the story and dialogue.

Cyberleek wasn't the only hacker to target Rockstar, either – there was also an enormous wave of GTA 6 leaks in 2022 – but even so, no baby boy and the driving force of the plot were plastered all over the internet as a result.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Anyway, however the bullet was dodged, it made for an excellent twist, and let Rockstar have the story moment it was hoping for. "It's meant to shock," Nelson explained. "We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason's character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end."

#4044. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#4043. 'The Results Are Very, Very Impressive' - Digital Foundry Praises GTA 6 On Xbox One

"﻿Latency is also exceptional - at least in context."

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

"Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair."

Performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones."

From their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

Streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

Latency also looks to be the big winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

"Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on."

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

Of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Can we just please appreciate what Microsoft offer here without triggering the Sony defence force? Cheerio 😁👍.

@Onlyboxmatters Wow, that is phenomenal fanboyism!

I tried it and came away impressed. After a few minutes it was easy to forget that it was being streamed.

I’m of two minds regarding this. On the one hand, hardware prices are outrageous. Ludicrously prohibitive for some. No one should ever be denied simply because they can’t afford a console to play on, so having the cloud streaming option for people who can’t budget for a new machine but may have an old relic of an XBone is a great thing.

On the other hand, for anyone who already has an S or X, choosing to stream this over the cloud instead of playing natively is just about the stupidest thing you could possibly do. It’s like you’re actively seeking ways to further remove yourself from the optimal experience. Why stop there? Why not set up a live camera feed pointed at your tv screen and send it to a tv in another room and play from there for maximum latency? By the time the input registers onscreen, GTA 7 should be out.

We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S

This is generally excellent. Though it is worth noting that YOUR mileage may vary with streaming. From previous Digital Foundry discussions Rich has very good full fibre (1GBps if I recall, with low ping) so this is a best case example.

However one major issue with streaming, compared to local play, is that everyone's performance is a little bit different, and if your ping is significantly worse, as most will be, then latency will also be a worse.

Never has YMMV (your mileage may vary) been more apt than with game streaming. Two different users can have entirely different results. Or the same user in two locations, or even on different days.

I don't look at Cloud as a primary way to play, but if I was in a situation where I had an XBO, and didn't like the prices of upgrading to a newer console just to play GTA VI, this would probably a good option.

Reality always ends up winning instead of what people would ideally do. With the price of consoles the way they are now I expect cloud gaming will become more and more viable for people that are cost conscious. Especially, if the cloud platform actually is viably working for gamers.

#4041. Pokémon Winds & Waves Release Date Speculation Rises From Gap In Anime Scheduling

We know that Pokémon Winds and Waves will launch on Switch 2 at some point in 2027, but that's it. The Pokémon Company is still keeping quiet about the upcoming Gen 10 entry, but an announced gap in the long-running anime has some people already narrowing the release window.

Earlier today, it was announced that the Pokémon anime would be taking a whopping nine-month gap between the finale of 'Winter Voyage' in December and a new series starring Liko and Roy, which kicks off in October 2027.

Serebii's Joe Merrick was quick to point out that the anime typically doesn't take breaks like this — usually airing an episode a week, bar some minor gaps. Given that new series of the show typically launch alongside their mainline game, does this mean that there has been a scheduling change at The Pokémon Company, with Winds and Waves being pushed back until later in the year?

For the entirety of my running Serebii there has been a new anime episode each week barring some gaps. For there to be none for 9 months is actually wild. Winds and Waves’ obvious schedule changes really messed with things huh

It certainly seems like a delay behind closed doors is possible — it is strange that TPC would schedule a gap this big in the anime run intentionally. If the upcoming series is set to tie in with Gen 10, then that would put Winds and Waves launching sometime around October 2027.

Hell, any extra time that TPC can be developing the next mainline title gets a big thumbs up from us.

Of course, it could also just be a wild intended pause in the anime, which had no sway on the game at all. TPC always eyes up the big pre-holiday November window for its mainline releases, so who's to say Gen 10 would ever have been any different?

Or things could be really off the wall, and this scheduled anime series is actually nothing to do with Winds and Waves, which TPC could go crazy and release any other time in the year instead!

In short, we're still waiting on something concrete from The Pokémon Company before we know the next release date for sure. But if this anime start date is anything to go by, we imagine we'll be seeing Gen 10 in the same November window that we're used to.

#4040. Path of Exile co-creator says "a shift back" to games like Baldur’s Gate 3 would be better for the industry

Larian has a purer relationship with the audience

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The industry's in a troubling position right now. Layoffs are widespread, triple-A budgets have ballooned, and it seems harder than ever to know what'll make a game stick. In the mind of one of the central devs on the Path of Exile series, Baldur's Gate 3 is a strong example of the kind of business model studios should aspire toward.

Chris Wilson, former lead designer on Path of Exile and co-founder of Grinding Gear Games, discussed the merits of Larian's approach with Destin on YouTube. "A like Baldur's Gate 3 is a great example of a very true game," he says.

"They made it, they had a good extended early access period for getting feedback without spoiling the game, and they released it in a sincere way," he explains. "Then, when given the opportunity to do more stuff for it, they said, actually, we want to make something else. That's cool, they'll make another thing, and that'll do well."

To his perception, "there's no manipulation there." Larian "got rewarded" appropriately and "everyone had a good time" in that transaction. "Sure, it's because it's an exceptionally good game," he adds. "But I think that a shift back to making games [like that] - it's less complicated, you can make more story-driven games. It doesn't have to be that everything is a live-service."

That's the million-dollar principle, really. Many games at the triple-A level simply don't need these features or mechanics, and Baldur's Gate 3 proves you can still have a close-to-one-to-one transaction between you and the player and be hugely successful.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and the Final Fantasy 7 remake trilogy are further examples. Wilson admits he probably wouldn't have made Path of Exile if they couldn't do it with live-service aspects, but that's because they were integral to the vision.

"It's designed around a big economy with lots of players, which is why it's free-to-play," he says. "It was very much designed to be live-service from the start."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

The current problem is games are being released with online elements "because the spreadsheet says it'll make more money," and the game is "contorted out of its single-player true experience" to facilitate these elements.

It must be said, it is refreshing still to play something and not have any online components to worry about or consider. Some games should just be their own experiences, and we need more of them - even if my to-play pile continues growing.

#4039. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#4038. The Witcher 4 Is Not a PS5 Exclusive, CDPR Clarifies After Sony Deal

Did anyone really think The Witcher 4 was going to be a PS5 exclusive?

For those who missed it, CDPR confirmed yesterday that it has signed a marketing deal with Sony on its upcoming RPG.

While the details are light, it’s expected this will take the same shape as PlayStation’s arrangement with GTA 6, where the title’s promoted “like” an exclusive – even though it’s technically not.

But it seems there was some confusion online about the nature of Sony’s deal, which CEO Michal Nowakowski has now clarified on social media.

“We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform.”

It’s as expected really, but Nowakowski still faced follow-up questions about whether Ciri’s story may launch first on PS5, before other platforms.

“All the platforms release at the same time: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. No one gets left behind.”

Of course, this is all entirely as expected – the original comments mentioned a marketing deal only, and I don’t think Sony could afford to keep a game as big as The Witcher 4 off other platforms, to be brutally honest.

It does hopefully mean the game will be optimised for the PS5, though, taking advantage of unique features like the DualSense et al.

I’m sure we’ll learn a lot more about how Sony and CDPR are collaborating once we get closer to the game’s release.

Historically, the PC store, GOG (Good Old Games) was created by CD Projekt, the Polish company best known for The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077. GOG launched in 2008 as a digital storefront focused on classic PC games and a "DRM-free philosophy", and it operated as part of the CD Projekt Group for over 17 years.

A lot of CD Projekt's games were sold on GOG, and GOG became well known for selling games 'without' DRM (Digital Rights Management) and for keeping older games working on modern PCs.

GOG has expressed interest in bringing back physical PC games, particularly the classic "big box" style releases.

So you'll find that while PlayStation as of 2027 (or whenever it is) no longer allows you have a physical game or DRM free; PC & Nintendo has much better ownership & DRM policies.

The situation is different now, CD Project RED learned from the Cyberpunk 2077 launch. They were using their own proprietary REDengine 4, which is a PC-first engine where console ports require a large amount of effort to get running and well optimized.

Now they are using Unreal Engine 5, which is a 3rd party engine built specifically for multi-platform releases. By design the engine takes care of many console porting efforts as it's an integral part of the engine. A developer from CD Project RED mentioned during a recent event that they are now designing games around the specifications of consoles rather than high-end PCs (like they did for Cyberpunk 2077).

So expect The Witcher 4 to run like any other Unreal Engine 5 game released recently (Clair Obscur Expedition 33, Saros, Silent Hill 2, Phantom Blade Zero, The Blood of Dawnwalker) on current platforms.

@TrollOfWar As a developer, I'm not only very familiar with Unreal Engine, I'm tremendously aware of how terrible it has been of late to work with effectively and efficiently.

I don't know of a developer or development team who is happy with the state of Unreal Engine right now. At this point I would assume those that are, are legally obliged to say so, or are receiving some financial benefit as a team for being aligned with it.

There is no such thing as a PC first engine, all game development engines run on PC first, and are built and incorporated around the implementation of console runtime environments using either SDK tools, Xbox/Nintendo/Sony DevTools or a combination of all or next to none.

As some terribly low budget Dev's will not have the SDK, select a drop down in Unity/Unreal Engine, export to the console and then have assistance from a platform suggested studio that assists, or an internal onboarding team.

So, a PC first engine simply means the developers are focused heavily on PC development as their primary bread and butter, it has nothing to do with the engine capabilities.

Unreal Engine itself is one of the most famous examples of PC first, as its engine literally was and is built around PC first ideology within development.

It's just marketed differently depending on which page of their site you click, which rep you speak to and so forth.

By going from REDengine, over to Unreal Engine, CDPR have not done so due to the ease at which they can deliver on console environments, it's due to the fact they clearly don't have the in-house technical staff to assist with incorporating all that is needed in a real-time environment into their engine. At least in an ongoing fashion during development, especially due to the dawn of at least 2-4 new consoles arriving in a year or two.

The issue is that Unreal Engine can be modified somewhat, it can be altered ad-hoc, yet ultimately all substantial feature sets and abilities are governed by their internal team of "specialists".

Lumen, Nanite, both wonderful, developers didn't get to implement that ahead of time, they didn't get to pick the time frame, they didn't get to choose how it speaks to the rest of the engine.

You lose a lot, a hell of a lot going from a very established, very capable engine runtime environment that your entire studio have spent years tailoring, to then go to an off the shelf solution with little to no say on the next major features and how they work alongside other tools.

There's a reason Pixar use Marionette and Render Man, it's not because it's easier, it's because every step of the way they get to not have to ask another company if they can "Please Sir have some more".

CDPR going from in house to off the shelf does not show they have learned anything, it shows their team quite literally don't know how to develop and maintain an in house engine during development of a cross-generational release.

People can believe what they think of the marketing speak, but I implore people to remember that we coming off the back of a few years of very terribly console optimised versions of releases that have indeed used Unreal Engine ... a PC first engine as they all are.

I will believe CDPR made the right decision for them when they prove it, up until now they have done everything but to the industry and consumers.

@dark_knightmare2 he doesn’t actually understand ownership rights so he thinks as long as you physically poses something you own it.

@ButteredCrumpet Interesting post. But I think there's a few things worth highlighting.

The main reason CDPR switched to Unreal Engine was stated in their debrief about why CyberPunk 2077 was delayed three times, and why even then it STILL came out in a poor state that required years of development to get it up to scratch. Their primary conclusions were related to the RED Engine, staff turnover and the issues these caused. (CDPR are very open and this was all in their investor calls)

That's not to say the RED Engine was bad, it isn't, but new staff would not be familiar with it, nor their custom tools, and many of their best devs would have to spend time getting the new staff up to speed, rather than actually working on the game. This slowed the whole process down considerably and reportedly caused some top staff to leave, which also didn't help. But it was made even worse because they also had a high staff turnover - for a variety of reasons - and so this process would repeat again and again, slowing progress to a crawl.

Interestingly 343 Industries came to exactly the same conclusion in their debrief as to why Halo Infinite was delayed a year, why it launched in an incomplete state, and again took years to bring many features expected at launch. Same conclusion: Bespoke engine and the issues this caused with a high staff turnover, hence they also decided to go UE5 before Halo was moved to Activision.

TLDR: Ultimately the decision for both studios was that for all the potential downsides of Unreal Engine the pros outweighed the cons.

What's particularly interesting is it isn't really about the technical capability of the engines, while that would have been a consideration, it's more about the people making it and the actual management issues of that when scaling up for these massive projects.

As the old saying goes, the best tool is the one you actually use.

The issue is that Unreal Engine can be modified somewhat

UE5 is almost entirely modular. You don't like the physics model, you don't like the lighting, the rendering or even major features like Lumen or Nanite you can replace them all.

Obviously at some point it makes no sense to, you might be better off building your own engine.

It will be interesting to see how CDPR will adapt UE5 for their uses. Like you I was slightly sceptical about using UE5 but will wait to see before judging. But I think it's fair to say most studios that release on UE5 don't have their own Engine Programmers who built something as complex as RED Engine, CDPR do, so they should be able to make the engine run better than most.

UPDATE: They even mentioned when working with Epic on the Witcher 4 demo that they had fixed some traversal stuttering bugs and sent those fixes back to Epic. CDPR aren't just licensing UE5, the engineers are rewriting core engine pipelines and contributing those fixes back into public versions of UE5 for the benefit of all developers.

#4037. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

Walmart's website is chock-full of all kinds of Black Friday deals; they're on items big and small, cheap and expensive, reliable and... not so much. I'm seeing a lot of gaming discounts on tech from brands I've never heard of.

I'm always looking to upgrade my gaming rig with the best tech out there, and I've browsed the Walmart Black Friday sales to see if the retailer has anything good on offer. It does, hidden under a heap of $20 RGB-toting controllers that look like they'd break after a single GTA 6 firefight, and here you'll find the top five picks I'd go for (if I had the money). Some of them are ways to improve my PC itself, others are things that'll let me game while I'm not at my desk.

It's not controversial to say that a good screen is fundamental for a great gaming experience. It's why I've picked a more premium option from Walmart's list: it has a more substantial discount, making it a bit easier to leap to the big-screen high-res model.

Why treat my rig to a premium experience, if I'm still going to spend every commute awkwardly fiddling with my phone screen to play games? I find mobile controllers a great buy for people who play a lot of shooters on their phone: they make you so much better, it feels like you're cheating.

I'm a big sucker for great-sounding immersive audio, and so I value a premium headset as one of the most important upgrades for any kind of gaming set-up. This is still an expensive piece of kit, but I wouldn't consider buying cheap headphones in case they ruin my games.

I've really become a convert to using a gaming controller on PC, and have enjoyed other GameSir products I've used. Plus, I find them more comfortable than the DualSense, so when I finally get a PS5, this controller will be ready for me.

What about a way to game on the go (while giving me access to a load of games not available on my PC?). This is the big Switch 2 discount of 2026's Black Friday, bundling Mario's racing game with the console and three months of Nintendo Switch Online.

I built my computer myself a good five years ago, and I did it in a pretty frustrating way, which was the only solution to my being low in funds at the time. I bought one or two components every Black Friday or Prime Day, and it took me well over a year to assemble all of the pieces.

Doing so saved me loads of money (at least a third of the price compared to buying the components outright), and I've come to defend Black Friday as a good time to upgrade parts of your gaming set-up which need some care. If you need something anyway, like a better monitor or replacement for a faulty item, you can get what you need at a discounted price.

I wouldn't buy a rig upgrade pre-emptively; if you think you might want a new headset in the near future, I'd always advise getting your money's worth and keeping your current model limping on as long as possible. I always wait until something's held together by string and duct tape before i upgrade, and discounts are pretty frequent anyway.

Also, if you've never owned an item on this list, like a mobile or PC controller, it's a good time to make that wish-list purchase. These items can sometimes fall into the 'want' category rather than the 'need' one, and the lower price makes it easier to justify the purchase.

#4033. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

#4032. Feature: 80+ PS5, PS4 Games to Buy in PS Store's Updated Black Friday Sale (North America/Europe)

PS5 and PS4 games going cheap we recommend

The PS Store's Black Friday sale is on now, running until 30th November, 2026.

As with nearly every offer in Sony's digital store, there are literally thousands of PS5 and PS4 games going cheap. Obviously, nobody has the time to scroll through all those deals, which is where this guide hopefully comes in handy.

We've put together a (relatively) shorter list of some of the games we'd highly recommend while they're on offer.

Everything listed here comes with at least a 7/10 score from Push Square, and every game is at its lowest price point, with some setting new lows in this sale.

Discounted prices are shown in bold, and games at a new lowest-ever price are bold and underlined.

If you need to top up your PSN wallet, we've got you covered:

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Let's have a look at some of the best games in the Black Friday sale.

The best James Bond game in a very long time, 007 First Light revives the character in brilliant style. Telling the origin story of the would-be spy, the game is a combination of sandbox-like, open-ended missions and linear set pieces and narrative moments, resulting in a highly appealing blockbuster. It tells a decent story, establishes fantastic new takes on well-known characters, and sets a solid foundation with great espionage and action gameplay.

1000xRESIST is all in on story, and this laser focus allows it to tell one of the most captivating and intriguing experiences you can have in video games. This sci-fi adventure sees an alien disease almost wipe out humanity, but one person is immune, and they rebuild society underground by cloning her. Combining visual novel elements with exploration, it's not the most challenging game to play, but its narrative more than makes it worthwhile.

If you're looking for a chilled out puzzle game to wind down with, A Monster's Expedition comes highly recommended. It's one of those puzzlers with a seemingly straightforward set of mechanics, but it uses them in increasingly smart ways to really test your brainpower. Set across hundreds of tiny islands you need to navigate by pushing logs into the water, its forgiving nature and gentle presentation make it a lovely game to get lost in.

A whimsical, miniature open world awaits in A Short Hike. From a top-down perspective, you explore an island with lots of interesting places to visit and adorable characters, each of whom has a task for you. This laid back experience is a true joy as you gain new abilities, collect things, and discover new areas.

Absolum is both a brilliantly crafted beat-'em-up and a devilishly addictive roguelike. Although the overall experience does feel slightly short-lived, you'll seriously struggle to tear yourself away from the game's striking fantasy world — especially when all of its systems start to click.

ARC Raiders is a phenomenal showcase of what immersive multiplayer can be. Every run is different, and your squad will come out with stories to tell each time. It can be tougher on those planning to play solo, and the extraction loop won't be for everyone. But as far as extraction shooters go, this is one of the most accessible, and it respects your time, giving you a fun experience from your first match. We can easily say that ARC Raiders is one of the best multiplayer games this generation.

Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is a delightfully inventive puzzle game that weaves in a neat narrative to pull you through. Playing as a character that literally moves the world around her as she goes, this is effectively a series of slide puzzles set within a fleshed out world full of whimsical character. Always building on its core idea in imaginative ways, this is brilliant fun from start to finish.

Building upon the great foundations laid in Astro's Playroom, Astro Bot is the full-blown 3D platformer the little robot deserves. It's an explosion of creativity and fun; there is something new to discover in practically every level, and all of it is purpose built to put a smile on your face. Not only is it bursting with imagination, it's also executed brilliantly. The controls are spot on, every new mechanic and power-up is fun to use, and it's all presented with incredibly sharp visuals and flawless performance. The icing on the cake is its celebration of PlayStation's past 30 years, with delightful nods to hundreds of classics. We can't recommend this highly enough.

While many of the included games may border on unplayable from a modern perspective, the painstaking attention to detail in Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is extremely easy to appreciate. The museum-like carousel of content, from interviews through to original artwork, is presented so handsomely that you can’t not get swept up in Atari’s dramatic story. And the fact that there over 100 of the company’s most famous titles, emulated excellently with their original instruction manuals available to pore over, adds playable context to a lot of the content. This is just an impressive overall experience that will appeal to those who lived through the rise (and fall) of Atari, as well as younger players eager to learn a little more about one of the industry’s true pioneers.

Avowed is arguably Obsidian's strongest modern release, and it's not for the reasons that you may think. While the game's writing and storytelling often lack bite and excitement, its gameplay saves the day with a cracking combat system, meaningful player choice, and the enjoyable exploration of some truly stunning locales.

Ball X Pit is a dangerously addictive roguelite that combines the speedy runs and rapid leveling up of Vampire Survivors with the ball-bouncing action of Breakout. It's one of those concepts that'll make you question why a game like it hasn't been done before, because it works brilliantly. Every element of the game feeds into something else, and the result is this incredibly compelling game that has a surprising amount to see and do.

Battle Chef Brigade Deluxe is the definitive version of this unusual but great culinary adventure. Set in a world where chefs go head-to-head in a prestigious cooking tournament, the game is half action title and half cooking minigames. You'll go out slaying monsters and harvesting ingredients, then brew them up to create delicious dishes to satisfy the judges. It's an odd recipe, but results in a surprisingly tasty dish.

Battlefield 6 is a phenomenal multiplayer experience that immerses and impresses with its chaotic mix of tight gunplay, best-in-class audio design, and the cinematic flair that made us love the series in the first place. The campaign isn’t anything to write home about, and Portal has yet to fully prove its worth, but they act as additions to what is easily the best Battlefield in over a decade.

A true cult classic, Beyond Good & Evil: 20th Anniversary Edition is a lovely remaster of a PS2 favourite. Playing as freedom fighter Jade, this unique sci-fi adventure has you exploring a weird and wonderful world through the lens of her camera. The remaster brings the visuals up to date and throws in some quality-of-life improvements, but the main reason to play this is for the great story and characters, which remain fresh and charming to this day.

Broken Sword: Shadow of the Templars is a sacred text in the history of point-and-click adventure games, and new remaster Reforged is the best version of the game that's ever been released. Quality-of-life improvements mean players who just want to enjoy the story without too much lateral thinking can do so, while veterans of the genre or returning fans can play the game in its original form, goats and all. Paris in the fall has never been more beautiful.

There have been climbing games before, but Cairn is a really unique example. To scale the huge Mount Kami, you need to control Aava's limbs individually, looking out for the best holds as you inch upward. On top of the challenging, physics-based mountaineering, you also need to keep on top of her health and hunger, but these survival aspects never feel too overbearing. It's a nicely balanced game with climbing that feels tangible and realistically tough.

Half interactive story, half cube-based puzzler, Catherine: Full Body is the expanded remaster of Atlus' brilliantly weird take on love. You play as Vincent, a 32-year-old bachelor who can't quite decide if he wants to commit to his long-term girlfriend. His potential infidelity gives way to suspiciously vivid nightmares where he's forced to scramble up towers made of blocks, lest he wake up dead. It's as mental as it sounds, but the tactile puzzles are addictive, and the storytelling is gripping at its best.

From the makers of TowerFall Ascension, Celeste is a pure platformer that provides a stern challenge. Using a straightforward set of moves, it does a lot with very little, but it's not just gameplay where it impresses. Madeline's climb up Celeste Mountain is both literal and metaphorical as she struggles to overcome her inner demons. Wonderfully pairing a touching story with rock solid platforming, this is one indie adventure that'll stay with you.

Creaks is one of PS4's very best puzzle games. Its commitment to continually evolving its mechanics makes for a phenomenal puzzling experience packed full of surprises and elating moments. With a stunning art style to boot as well as a narrative which reveals itself in all the right ways, Creaks offers an unforgettable ride that can be considered truly special.

Some say there are too many Metroidvania games for this world, yet when one as good as Crypt Custodian comes along, it serves as a reminder of exactly why so many developers chase that addictive fusion of explorative action. With shades of Death's Door and Tunic, brotherly duo Kyle and Eric Thompson have made an approachable yet exceedingly enjoyable adventure full of combat, platforming, puzzles, and charm.

Masterful in its storytelling, characters, and visuals, Kojima Productions went bigger and better with a sequel that comfortably dwarfs what the Japanese team achieved in its first delivery experience. Main character Sam is once again tasked with reconnecting a land mass to the chiral network, but this time his deliveries are further and expanded to encompass proper combat scenarios. Death Stranding 2 is a cinematic achievement on all fronts that will remain one of the crown jewels of the PS5 library forever.

Stephen has been part of the Push Square team for over six years, bringing boundless enthusiasm and a deep knowledge of video games to his role as Assistant Editor. Having grown up playing every PlayStation console to date, he's developed an eclectic taste, with particular passion for indie games, arcade racers, and puzzlers. He's also our go-to guy for Sonic-related matters, much to his delight/chagrin.
