#4031. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4030. Team Cherry Uses The Pull Of Silksong To Highlight A Trio Of Wonderful-Looking Indies

Just when we thought that we couldn't have any more respect for Team Cherry, the dev goes and uses its platform to highlight even more adorable-looking indies coming out of Australia.

The Cherry Time! showcase promised "a bunch of exciting announcements," and these were not Hollow Knight-related (until the last one, of course), but instead focused on a handful of titles coming out under the studio's publishing arm.

We've got the trailer and info for each of the three games included below, but honestly, what a wholesome way for Team Cherry to use its indie power! We came for Silksong DLC news (and we got it), but we left with another three games to add to our wishlists.

All of the following are listed as "Currently in development" at the time of writing, and none have been confirmed for Switch yet. That said, given the success Team Cherry has seen on the platform with Hollow Knight and Silksong, we'd be amazed if they don't extend the publishing our way at some point.

So, let's meet the three games highlighted in the show...

On this page: Team Cherry Uses The Pull Of Silksong To Highlight A Trio Of Wonderful-Looking Indies

Solve a grand mystery atop a gigantic walking city in Blokkan: Secret of the Walking City! Gather clues, meet eccentric characters, and solve playful puzzles in an unforgettable adventure

Moody lofi beats meet playful platform adventuring in a ruined, rainy world! Search rain-spattered streets, take on an army of mischievous creatures, and work together with your spirit companion to find a way home

Solve a planet-spanning plant mystery as the interstellar botanist Hatti and her trusty translator, Oliver! Investigate a lush, natural world and befriend a cast of crazy creatures in this breezy, beautiful adventure

After all that, the dev wrapped up with a closer look at the Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow DLC, confirming that it'll launch on Switch and Switch 2 on 11th December. You'll find all the details on that trailer in our coverage below.

#4029. 19 Of This Year's Best Xbox Games Now Have Free Trials For All Players

Star Wars: Galactic Racer being the latest one

It's been an amazing year for new releases on Xbox, and something you might not be aware of is that many of those games also come with free trials, allowing you to see whether you're willing to commit to a full purchase.

We've highlighted some of these before, but there are new ones as well - the incredible Star Wars: Galactic Racer has literally just added a free trial this week. Most of these trials include the full game but are limited to a couple of hours (sometimes more) before they lock you out, but that's plenty of time to discover whether you're a fan or not!

There are some exceptions where trials are provided in the form of demos or a "Starter Pack", so we'll be sure to mention those in the list below. We've gone through the top 50 Xbox games of 2026 based on Metacritic's rankings, so anything you see below is (according to them) one of the best 50 Xbox releases of the year.

For anything that's listed here as a "free trial", you'll want to go to the Microsoft Store app on your Xbox console and locate the game in question, where a "free trial" button should appear next to the ability to buy it.

All the other demos and separate things like a "Starter Pack" are standalone items on the Xbox Store, so if you search for "007 First Light - Free Starter Pack", for example, that's where you'll find the free trial for that game.

Here are a couple of examples to help you with this:

Many of these titles are also available in the Xbox Black Friday Sale right now, so if you're not too busy with GTA 6 and fancy trying some of these out, you might just be able to decide whether it's worth buying the full versions at a discount.

We wish Xbox did a better job at making it clear when new trials have arrived on the Xbox Store, so hopefully that's something that might be addressed in 2027. For now, hopefully this list proves useful for the Pure Xbox community!

Avengers: Doomsday is now just around the corner and sees Simu Liu return as Shang-Chi for the first time in five years. The star, who last appeared in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, will join the fight against Doctor Doom in the upcoming Marvel Phase 6 movie.

Not too much is known yet about his storyline in the new movie, but we have seen a glimpse of his fight with Channing Tatum's Gambit in the trailer. Teasing the upcoming skirmish, Liu says they tried to make it as practical as they could.

"To have a scene partner like Channing [Tatum], who is as insistent as I was about getting to do as much of it as possible, was critical to the success of that scene," Liu told Entertainment Weekly. "It was cool to have a dance partner who was as down to get into it as I was. There’s a lot of valid criticisms about the use of CGI in movies and everything, but for what it's worth, I think we really strived to make that sequence in particular as practical as it possibly could have been."

This isn't the only fight scene that we've had an insight into ahead of Doomsday. A new TV spot showing Magneto and Doom facing off on the battlefield as the iconic X-Men star tried to rip Doom's mask off his face. It's fair to say it didn't go to plan.

#4027. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#4026. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

#4025. PS Plus Essential's Next Update Looks a Bit Better in Japan Than the Rest of the World

It’s all subjective, of course, but Japan’s PS Plus Essential update for December 2026 looks a little bit better than what we’re getting in the west.

Now if we’re looking at pure value here, the Japanese lineup is objectively better: the Bleach game retails for $59.99, while Amnesia is $24.99. The former is also available on PS5 and PS4, whereas the latter is only available for PS4 (although you can of course play it on PS5 via backwards compatibility).

Bleach is also newer, having released in 2025, while Amnesia is from 2023.

But it does ultimately all come down to taste, I suppose; survival horror fans may be much happier with Frictional’s title – especially if they have no real interest in anime. I suppose the lineup in Japan does lack variety, as you’re getting two very similar titles from Bandai Namco there.

Amnesia: The Bunker did release in Japan, so I’m not entirely sure why the lineup is different between regions.

Sony is putting a lot of marketing into its domestic region at the moment, as it tries to reverse its flagging fortunes. It’s also just launched a new PS Portal there, and is putting a pretty big promotional campaign behind it. Maybe it thinks this lineup will be more enticing to Japanese players.

Interesting stuff, though, which selection would you have preferred? I’ve had the Bleach game on my wishlist for a little while, so I think I would have rather got that – but I can certainly see why people would prefer the more varied worldwide selection as well.

#4024. Feature: Eight Rockstar Xbox Games That Are Still Playable With Backwards Compatibility

Specifically from the original Xbox and Xbox 360 eras

With GTA 6 taking up so much attention on Xbox and PS5 right now, it's no surprise that we're also seeing a spike in interest for the likes of GTA 4 and other classic entries from the series that have appeared on Xbox over the years.

The same goes for most of Rockstar Games' titles on the platform, such as the two amazing Red Dead Redemption releases, and that's got us thinking about all the amazing games the studio has managed to produce.

Xbox has a really big bonus here in the form of backwards compatibility, allowing us to play Rockstar's titles from the original Xbox and Xbox 360 eras, so those are the ones we thought we'd focus on for this feature specifically.

So, here we go! Here are eight Rockstar Xbox games that still work to this day through backwards compatibility:

While it might feel like a bit of a shock to the system to go back to GTA 4 after playing GTA 6, it arguably has the best story in the entire series, and you're doing yourself a disservice if you don't at least give it a go! The game also ended up getting two single-player DLCs in the form of The Lost & Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, both of which are also playable via Xbox backwards compatibility. Just keep in mind that GTA 4 could really do with a visual boost on Xbox Series X and S, and here's hoping it gets a free upgrade at some point in the future.

The first two legendary Max Payne titles were developed by Control studio Remedy Entertainment, but they were published by Rockstar Games. If you want something that reminds you a bit more of GTA and Red Dead in terms of gameplay feel, it might be worth checking out the Rockstar-developed Max Payne 3. I've personally never played this one, but have consistently heard that it's an underrated gem from Rockstar's back-catalogue.

You probably don't need us to say anything about RDR - Red Dead Redemption is an absolute classic from 2010 that has a lot in common with GTA 4 in terms of how it plays, and if you're into something a bit more slow-paced with a ton of atmosphere and an incredibly memorable campaign, it's well worth picking up. Anyone who bought this digitally can get a free Series X and S upgrade, but the physical Xbox 360 version still functions via backwards compatibility.

Listen, it might sound ridiculous to consider buying a table tennis game if you're not massively into the sport, but Rockstar's take on it is probably the best version of non-VR ping-pong we've ever seen in video game form. There's a ton of depth here, the graphics are fantastic for 2006, and this crucially served as Rockstar's first ever release using their new "RAGE" game engine, which is the one that was also used for GTA 6... 20 years later!

Bully (also known as Canis Canem Edit) is essentially like taking Grand Theft Auto and scaling it down into a school environment. It does have its own kind of feel and style compared to the GTA games, but you'll feel right at home playing as Jimmy Hopkins as he attempts to navigate his way around a school full of utter imbeciles!

There are loads of Midnight Club games that are worth your attention, and Los Angeles isn't necessarily the best of them all, but it's the only one featured in the Xbox backwards compatibility program. It's still a really good racing game that features a big open-world map that'll remind you of GTA 5, and there's ultimately a lot of fun to be had here. The only real downside is that it remains locked at 30FPS on Xbox One, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

Red Dead Revolver is the often overlooked first game in the Red Dead series, and that's because it plays very differently to the other two and only received lukewarm reviews at launch in 2004. You have to go into this one with the right expectations, but some would say it's underrated, and it's certainly worth considering if you're eager for more Red Dead in your life. It also seems to run at up to 4K, 60FPS on Xbox Series X, and 60FPS on Series S too.

GTA has always been considered one of the most controversial franchises of all time, but Rockstar Games outdid themselves in the controversy department when Manhunt released in 2003. This is a brutal game in which you play as a death row inmate, and it's so violent that it ended up getting banned in multiple countries. I've personally never played this one, but it has a 74/100 rating for Xbox over on Metacritic, while the Xbox Store (US) version has a 4.8/5 rating based on those who have played it via backwards compatibility.

Beyond these, we also want to give a special mention to L.A. Noire (which was released on Xbox 360 but nowadays has a native Xbox One version on the Xbox Store) and Grand Theft Auto's Trilogy Definitive Edition, the latter of which isn't necessarily the best to play GTA 3, Vice City and San Andreas, but is certainly the most accessible.

We've had seven years to think about it. We've got Robert back, greatest actor in the world. I think it is unlike any movie that's been made in the Marvel universe up to this point. It's tonally very different. It's very surprising. I think the audience is going to be very surprised when they see the movie.November 26, 2026

Joe Russo also recently had high praise for another Marvel actor: Tom Holland. "I think Tom Holland translates in a way that I don't know if very few actors in history translate," he shared. "There is a charm and a genuineness and a warmth to him that really resonates with audiences. And he's so authentic as a person and his performances are so authentic, and he really embodies that character in a way that's straight off the page of the comics.

"And I think that movie is a testament to his star power," he continued. "We've said this before, he's the last great movie star. There's a vintage quality to Tom Holland that feels like it comes from a time that doesn't exist now. There's lots of great movie stars out there, but [his] energy is different. He's got that quality that very, very few people have had."

However, Tom Holland is not confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday as he was left out of Marvel's supersized casting reveal. Whether we'll see him again in Avengers: Secret Wars or not remains to be seen.

The latest (and final) Doomsday trailer sees Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom go up against the Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Thunderbolts, and it focuses heavily on Chris Evans's Steve Rogers. It turns out Steve's decision to go back in time to live with Peggy Carter at the end of Avengers: Endgame has triggered the incursions threatening the multiverse in Doomsday…

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Doomsday arrives this December 18. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else that's on the way.

#4021. The Witcher 3 Remastered Patch 5.02 Fixes Annoying PS5 Stutters, Improves Performance, and Much More

The Witcher 3 Remastered has a new update on PS5, and it's available to download right now, weighing in at a reasonable 1.6GB.

Patch 5.02 is the one many have been waiting for, as it addresses the game's most annoying technical issue on console. I am, of course, referring to the momentary stutters that occurred when autosave was triggered.

This problem was especially noticeable when quest information popped up on the screen, both when you began a quest and finished it. Thankfully, CD Projekt Red's finally taken action.

The patch also improves v-sync and VRR "behaviour" on PS5, which should result in a smoother overall experience. Screen flickering has also been addressed.

On top of those more-than-welcome adjustments, the update is packed with bug fixes — some of which are related to the remaster's new lighting techniques, which could result in some areas looking poorly or incorrectly illuminated.

And in terms of gameplay, we're looking at a bunch of balancing tweaks to a number of Geralt's skills. Some of these perks simply weren't being calculated properly, so you should be more effective in combat right out of the gate with this update installed.

Gravity Well, founded in 2020 as an "anti-crunch" game studio, lost its funding earlier this year and wasn't able to find a new backer.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation."

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

#4018. GTA 6 Gives PS5 a Very Rare Win Over Switch 2 in Japan

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

This is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it shows that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The company’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the new Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

#4017. Yooka-Laylee Developer Issues Statement On Why Definitive Edition Is Skipping Xbox

"...just isn't viable for us at this time"

Digital Foundry's John Linneman has also weighed in on this:

Original Story: Yesterday, we published an article about how Xbox fans were making their voices heard regarding a lack of Definitive Edition upgrade for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair, and we've now got an official statement about it.

In a post on social media, developer Playtonic Games explained that "the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time", and that they've had to "prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs".

Here's the full statement that was shared by the studio:

"Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th. We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision.

Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure, and we can't wait for new and returning players alike to experience the Impossible Lair on these platforms for the first time. Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future.

We understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback."

Based on this, it only sounds like there's a slim chance of getting the Definitive Edition upgrade of Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair on Xbox, but who knows whether it could end up being added down the line.

For what it's worth, the game already runs and plays well on Xbox One, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it's obviously a bummer when other platforms are getting enhanced visuals and up to 120FPS as part of this upgrade.

It is what it is! We'll just keep enjoying the 2019 version instead.

#4016. Frodo star Elijah Wood calls out "AI BS" as a "first look" at Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum goes viral

The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum has wrapped filming, but we're still yet to see a proper first look at our favorite characters returning. However, that hasn't stopped fake images of the movie circulating online, which Frodo star Elijah Wood has been quick to point out.

An online publication posted on Twitter what it called the "first look behind the scenes images" of the upcoming film. This featured mock-ups of Lee Pace's return as Thranduil, Ian McKellen back as Gandalf the Grey, and Wood as Frodo Baggins, as well as what it branded as the first look at Jamie Dornan as Aragorn and Anya Taylor-Joy as Seren.

It's pretty clear they are AI-mock-ups as they feature strange, uncanny details like changing coffee cup sizes and odd expressions on faces, but Wood wanted to make sure fans knew they were fake. Posting on Twitter he replied to the images writing, "this is AI BS". Following his post, the social media site has now added a label confirming the detail.

The only official images we've had of the upcoming Lord of the Rings movie come from a behind-the-scenes video posted by Warner Bros. Shared in September, these feature new looks at the Shire as well as a glimpse at the back of Frodo's head.

Andy Serkis recently shared another glimpse at the set to mark the end of filming. While this didn't contain any footage from the movie, it did feature the actors' Gollum voice once again.

The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum hits theaters December 17, 2027, the same day as Avengers: Secret Wars. For more, check out our guide to how to watch the Lord of the Rings movies in order.

#4015. Hitman, 007 First Light PS5 Crossover Makes Lenny Kravitz Your New Ally

It's a bit surprising this crossover hasn't already happened, to be honest, given IO Interactive is the studio behind both of the games, but it's now been confirmed a Hitman and 007 First Light collaboration is happening.

The content is live from today until 24th December 2026, and it takes the form of a new Elusive Target in Hitman. Lenny Kravitz, who is playing Bawma from 007 First Light, is the next celebrity to feature in Hitman, but this time, he's on Agent 47's side.

Bawma has been betrayed by three of his associates, and he's called in the bald assassin to take them down.

Up for elimination are Horace Stockton, Oswald Spoon, and Zui.

The new set of Elusive Targets and the mission hosting them brings with it the likeness and voice of Lenny Kravitz, who you'll hear from throughout the level via Agent 47's earpiece.

"Bawma is such a fun and interesting character to portray, so I was excited to step back into a new world with him for 007 First Light," said Kravitz. "Seeing Bawma team up with Agent 47 is something I think fans of both games are going to love."

The mission will be available until 24th December, but if you own a copy of the game, then you'll retain permanent access to the Arcade version of it. It can also be accessed free of charge for those who don't have Hitman 3, as it's being added to the demo of the game.

Review Hitman 3 (PS5) - The Ultimate Stealth Sandbox

Alongside the mission, a roadmap detailing the Season of Bawma teases the following content additions: a new Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, a new challenge, a batch of Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop and an IOI Account reward.

Will you team up with Lenny Kravitz to take down his associates? Let us know in the comments below.

Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.

It ain’t over ’til it’s fibre wire around your neck over.

I am still waiting for that First Light story dlc.

#4014. My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

Longing for the Venetian Dogehouse, stuck in the Venetian doghouse

The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching new lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

This is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

Getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

If you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

When you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your company can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

If you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a new branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

In the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

As the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

Thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for said Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

Not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the big chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing new folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

Thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a new piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

While I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

But Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

With federal agents and the best bounty hunters in the nation massing on their heels, the gang must rob, steal and fight their way across the rugged heartland of America in order to survive. As deepening internal divisions threaten to tear the gang apart, Arthur must make a choice between his own ideals and loyalty to the gang who raised him.

Discover the breathtaking landscapes of Japan in over 550 real-world cars and become a racing Legend at the Horizon Festival. Start your journey as a tourist and explore a world full of hit music and Japanese culture. Build a Valley Estate, acquire awe-inspiring homes, and display your prized car collection in fully Customizable Garages. Cruise the roads with your friends and join Car Meets around Japan, unleash your imagination with EventLab and build together in Horizon CoLab.*

EA SPORTS™ UFC® 6 is powered by fighters. Evolved striking and motion systems bring those UFC stars to life in the Octagon, while new game modes introduce immersive storytelling that makes every fight feel personal. That starts with Markerless Capture, which delivers unprecedented fighter fidelity with authentic locomotion and Signature Strikes, complemented by new fighter bodies built with Sapien Technology that make your favorite UFC superstars truly look, move, and fight like themselves.

#4010. Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone

New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

There's nothing forcing you to do any of this in company, mind. "Stay a mysterious shadow, lend a hand when you feel like it, and disappear before anyone can make it weird," the devs explain, adding a hug emoji to make plain that they don't think you're some kind of smelly misanthrope for shunning other players.

I, personally, am a smelly misanthrope, and will only ever appear in your game as a skulking opacity, peering through the window of your personal gingerbread house, with its tastefully accessorised lava lamps and throw rugs. No, I will not join you for a group hang-glider tour. No, I do not want to play the banjo with you. You will experience me only as the nagging sensation of being watched, while you chat to the local "Stylesmith" about fetching rucksack patterns.

Spirit Crossing has an upfront cost that "gives players full access to the complete game experience in perpetuity", but you can also take out a subscription for some cosmetic items and access to a "limited resource exchange shop". They're avoiding traditional microtransactions, which is nice.

Spry Fox are also the developers of Cozy Grove - "the best grove since Byker", wrote Graham, in one of his regular 'senior moments'. I myself know them as the studio behind wintry puzzler Road Not Taken, with its randomised woodlands, and block-merging city builder Triple Town, with its unexpectedly terrifying bears. Little about Spirit Crossing seems terrifying, unless you count the shadow loitering at the edge of your conversation pit.

You can read more about the game on Steam. I find Spirit Crossing quite novel, especially when it dispenses with the WholeCosy "discover your inner fashonista" stuff and leans into the supernatural elements: I like the idea of hunkering by the campfire during a storm, watching the clouds hurtle past. Still, I'm disappointed to hear that Spry Fox have made use of generative AI during its creation.

As has been pointed out to us on Bluesky, the developers called on Anthropic's Claude tools for various behind-the-scenes tasks - the example they give in a Discord post is editing several config files at once. There's no disclosure on the game's Steam page because Spry Fox haven't used AI tools to generate any of the art or music - Valve rewrote Steam's disclosure requirements in January to exempt the usage of generative AI for "efficiency gains", which the above presumably falls under.

It's hardly a full-throated endorsement of generative AI, but it still forms part of a political and cultural project I consider reckless and morbid. For a longer account of my objections, albeit one that doesn't cover Claude in particular, here's my longform thinkywangle from July last year.

How to get permanent boosts to your max Health, Stamina, and Focus in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Missions that permanently boost max Health, Stamina, and Focus in GTA 6 appear in a few places. However, you'll never know there's a buff until you complete them and all but one are hidden away, meaning you'll need to find them by chance or get lucky.

As well as being worth seeking them out if you want to buff your stats, they also include some of the best and weirdest missions in the game, so it's a double win if you do go after them. I've not included the meditation spots in GTA 6 that also boost your max Focus here, as that's a whole thing in its own right.

The map above shows where you you start each mission. Some are single hit jobs where you do one thing and get the boost, others require a few steps and you might have to wait to continue.

I've covered the whole GTA 6 aliens thing fully already, but the short version is you need to be abducted (the map shows where it happened for me), by looking out for an abandoned car at night with all its light flashing. After that you need to sleep, where a dream will show you the rest of the way. Read my full guide for all the details but completing this will permanently increase your Health, Stamina, and Focus

The GTA 6 Final Flush mission can be started by scanning the QR code you find in the bathroom marked above. It's at Corsair Key, near where you start the game. Once you've done that you'll get a second marker to meet someone at a waffle house. Read our guide for the full walkthrough, but at the end of it you'll come out with a permanent increase in max Stamina.

This is the only mission that's pointed out to you when you scan the crop dusting poster outside the motel reception in chapter 2. This will direct you to McKittrick Farm marked on the map above. You'll need to dust the crops first but that will then lead to a mission later where you need to get some chemicals. Complete that and you'll have the chance to eat a mutated strawberry that will permanently increase your max Stamina. You'll get a text later to close out this mission and, while there are no more stat boosts, I highly recommend seeing how it all ends.

The Circles of Hell mission sees you visit Satan and blow him away Doom style. You'll need to find the garage marked above in Port Gellhorn somewhere around midnight. You'll know it's the right time because it'll be open and lit up red. Talk to the people inside and go with them to meet the dark lord and kill him. If you fail at all at this point, check the wooden throne for some more 'shrooms so you can try again. Defeat the hordes and you'll get a permanent increase to your max Health, plus a shotgun and t-shirt.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

If you head all the way out to Lake Tallaloko north of Milliport you'll find a logging yard full of felled trees. Make your way to the location on the map and you'll find a yellow shipping crate you can enter. At least one person here at GR reported needing the cut-off tool in GTA 6 to open it, but when I found it (before having the tool) it was just open. Inside you'll find a mysterious psychedelic box you can interact with. Do that and you'll have to complete a trippy obstacle course made of crates and logs. Get through it and you'll get a permanent max Stamina increase and new tattoo.

Head roughly to this area on the map (near where you can get abducted by aliens at night) and listen out for shouting and gunfire in the woods, near the road construction site. Here you’ll find a group of self-proclaimed ‘ecologists’ doing some environmental hunting of invasive species. Pick up the Duke 556 Assault Rifle on the barrel to begin the ‘practice round’ shooting static targets such as pumpkins, and then you’ll be prompted to wager $250 on the main challenge - shooting a bunch of iguanas released from a cage. Win and you'll get $250 plus a max Focus increase.

#4007. Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

How an unconventional peripheral became an equally unexpected survivor

PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.

Unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95. At E3 later that May, Microsoft demonstrated the Strategic Commander for the first time with SimCity 3000, while promoting its potential for other such games as Diablo II, Warcraft III, and Baldur's Gate II. This was all taking place during the so-called 'Golden Age of Real-Time Strategy Games,' which spanned roughly from the mid-1990s to the mid-2000s. It was when the RTS genre was at the peak of its mainstream popularity, and we fans were devoted to mastering its intricacies in any way we could to have a competitive edge.

Microsoft, all the while, were taking notes. "The team conceived the Strategic Commander in the late 1990s," Carl Ledbetter - then Industrial Design Manager for Microsoft's PC Hardware Group, now Head of Design for Xbox Devices - recalls to me. "As RTS games grew in popularity, we saw an interesting opportunity to design a new physical interface around a new interaction model. The idea was for it to be used left-handed in concert with right-hand PC desktop mouse control. We wanted to enable players to perform faster with more fluidity, comfort, optimised control placement for multiple hand sizes, simplicity of set-up, and ease of programming."

For Ledbetter and co. to realise this ambition, the Strategic Commander was designed as a unique combination of mouse, joystick, and gamepad. To manage the increasing complexities of the RTS games of the day, it came equipped with six programmable buttons, three shift buttons, and a three-position profile switch. Back then, these atypical features provided an unprecedented 72 possible key combinations across various configurations, all at the tip of our stubby little fingers. Better yet, it allowed us to toggle between three pre-configured profiles at a time, so that we could switch up our configurations on the fly depending on which stage of an RTS match we were in.

On release, contemporary reviewers acknowledged its originality, with critics like ActiveWin's Julien Jay describing it as "probably the most innovative (with the GameVoice) and revolutionary" peripheral designed specifically for strategy players. Others, like Neoseeker's Arnel Lim, suggested that it might’ve gone overboard with its customisation options, saying "you won't use anywhere close to all of them," in reference to the controller's programmable key combinations. Either way, the Strategic Commander failed to supplant conventional peripherals in the hands of most RTS players, and it was discontinued in 2003. As was the rest of the original SideWinder line, owing to declining sales and the industry-wide shift toward standard M+K setups for all PC games and genres.

However, unlike so many of its Microsoft-made siblings, this was not the end for the Strategic Commander. Niche as it was, it went on to enjoy a surprisingly long post-shelf life, one that was stretched out by a dedicated cult following - and that continues to this day. But why? Why, after all these years, is this forgotten peripheral from a discontinued line maintaining such a enthusiastic fanbase, years after the industry around it had written it off as a failure?

The answer lies in software and OS compatibility, as much as the hardware's own appeal. Andreas Weis was the developer of one of the first unofficial patches for the Strategic Commander, allowing players to keep on using it even after the original software stopped being compatible with newer versions the Windows. By that point, the device was a decade old, and well into 'official' obsolescence, yet Weis still answered the call of the Strategic Commander's righteously frustrated - if numerically few - fans. "There was a lot of interest back in the early 2010s in software patches to keep the Strategic Commander functional when the original software for the Strategic Commander stopped working," he explains. "Users were asking around on internet forums about how to get it to work on Windows 7 and Vista machines. Since I was studying computer science at the time, I was quite interested in reverse-engineering, and I hacked together a simple tool that would cover my use cases for the device."

In the years that followed, other patches were released to keep the Strategic Commander operational, the most notable of which was Philip Merwarth’s Strategic Engine software in 2013. Unfortunately, they weren’t open-source. Worse was that the protocol for programming the Strategic Commander wasn’t documented anywhere online in a way that was accessible for users. This is why Weis realized that he could make a unique contribution.

"I polished my old prototype code for the Strategic Commander software patch and released it as a library, so that other people could use it to write their own applications for programming the tool," he says. "As for me, I released one application that made use of the library publicly, the vJoy feeder application, which allows the device to be used with games that support joystick inputs." Curiously, Weis, by this time and like many others, had found other applications for a device with such a specific selling point, and even continues to use the Strategic Commander sparingly in 2026.

"The production quality of Microsoft hardware at the time was just top-notch, and I love the design of the old SideWinder devices, which is why I did not just throw the thing out when the software stopped working," he tells me. "It was worth keeping around to find new uses for it over the years, and I eventually realized that it makes quite a nice addition to a HOTAS (Hands-On Throttle And Stick) setup, where I could put actions that aren’t time-critical and don't fit well on the throttle on the Strategic Commander instead. For example, when I’m playing Elite Dangerous in VR, I’d put actions like deploying the landing gear on the Strategic Commander to free up buttons on the throttle for actions that were more relevant for combat."

When looking back at the history of Microsoft’s SideWinder line, it’s easy to call the Strategic Commander a failed experiment, given the fact that most of us are still using the same standard mouse-and-keyboard setup to play RTS games. However, the central premise behind its design philosophy was that the interface between a player and a game could be redesigned to cater to specific genre quirks, and decades following its release, it’s still maintained a coalition of loyal users: some RTS players who believed the Strategic Commander really pulled it off, and those found other uses for the device in other flavours of PC game. And with the issue of modern compatibility, a roadblock for so much retro hardware, bypassed by homemade patches, both camps can continue twisting and clicking their Strategic Commanders unimpeded.

All the same, I wonder if it might have basked in more conventional success, had Microsoft made more forward-thinking decisions. The Strategic Commander has proven over the years that its unprecedented customisation had applications far beyond what Ledbetter’s team had envisioned, and once the popularity of RTS games settled down, other, similar click-heavy subgenres like MOBAs and Real-Time Tactics got big as well. Would a more officially maintained, potentially refined Strategic Commander model have served those crowds? I think it might. The narrow focus on RTS games may have also hurt the device's since-demonstrated broader appeal; if Microsoft had fully capitalised on this customisation selling point by communicating its benefits to everyone, not just those playing the single most popular PC genre at the time, it could have provided the blueprint for a proper, long-lived alternative to controllers, mice, and keyboards.

Alas, gaming history is littered with revolutionary peripherals that failed to actually revolutionise the industry surrounding them. The Strategic Commander is no different, but for the fact that it’s had this surprisingly long post-shelf life - and, as a result, the opportunity for insight into what could have been done to salvage the its failures. Still, that unexpected longevity can provide come comfort to the Strategic Commander's creators, as well as its lingering users.

"I think the design made sense for its time, especially with the rising popularity of RTS games," Ledbetter reflects. "Looking back, I would have liked more time to test and refine the Strategic Commander. I’m proud of what we brought to market, and I’m glad to know that it remains beloved by many players to this day."

There are tons of unique and collectible weapons in GTA 6 but these are the best and easiest to snap up early in the game.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38

This is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

Another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

This Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.

#4005. Feature: Everything You Need to Know Ahead of the Delta Force Invitationals Grand Final

The tactical shooter’s 3-day LAN championship kicks off in Sweden this weekend - with huge in-game rewards for tuning in

After last year’s inaugural event in Hangzhou, this weekend sees the Delta Force Invitational make its first move outside Asia, as an official competitive title at DreamHack in Stockholm, Sweden, from 27th-29th November. The Grand Final of the tournament will take place on November 29th at 11am UTC+0 through to 4pm UTC+0 after three days of global competitive action.

It’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows:

Fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. Alliance, being a Swedish team, will be playing on home soil, but only time will tell if this gives them an additional boost. They, and the ten other teams to have gone the distance, will once again be competing for a share of a $500,000 prize pool.

One core aspect of Delta Force that’s attracted new fans over the last twelve months is its commitment to extraction as an esport. Whereas in traditional FPS competitions there’s an obvious focus on winning fights, in Delta Force’s Operations mode, information gathering, firefights, resource management and extraction decisions all play out within a single match.

Viewers who tune in to watch on Twitch via @DeltaForceGameOfficial or @DeltaForce_Esports can also bag a bunch of in-game rewards:

Plus, GOTAGA, HutchMF, Summit1G, Panda and Timmy will also be streaming the matches on their channels during the event.

There’s also a tonne of in-game incentives around the event, so be sure to login between the 11th November and 3rd December to get your hands on these:

If you correctly predict the outcome of the Invitational in-game, there’s a couple of other other rewards to be had:

In the two years since its launch, Delta Force has steadily gained momentum, with developers Team Jade determined to grow the tactical FPS into a globally recognised esports title. With three days of intense competition on the horizon, its future certainly looks bright.

Delta Force is free to play and available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Android, iOS, Google Play, Epic Games Store, and Steam.

James Marsden says his comic-accurate Cyclops suit in Avengers: Doomsday gives the audience “everything that they want to see" – even if the actor might not be feeling so snug after stepping out of the black leather.

“The comic-accurate suit was very exciting for me to do, but [they] still haven’t figured out the comfort thing yet,” Marsden told Entertainment Weekly of his brightly colored ensemble piece, which largely mirrors the X-Men leader's traditional wear.

“No, it was great. It was one of those pinch-me moments where you’re playing this iconic character and then coming back and giving the fans everything that they want to see.”

Famously, the original X-Men trilogy cracked a joke at the expense of the superhero group's colorful array of costumes. When Hugh Jackman's Wolverine grumbled about the black leather in 2000's X-Men, Cyclops deadpanned if he would prefer "yellow spandex" instead.

In recent years, Marvel Studios has given the X-Men its due on the costume front. Deadpool and Wolverine not only featured Logan in his traditional yellow and blue outfit, but also dealt Gambit a winning hand with his comic book-style suit.

With Disney's acquisition of Fox, Kevin Feige – who had a behind-the-scenes production role on the first X-Men – is finally able to make his cinematic universe dreams come true, with even Marsden admitting there had been "so much chatter" in the past about bringing the mutant team to the MCU.

So, costume? Check. A fully-fledged role instead of nostalgia bait? Check. A leading light in the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, complete with iconic catchphrase? Check, check, and check. If you're a Cyclops fan, you'll be eating well this holiday season.

#4003. Judge denies motion to dismiss lawsuit accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of worsening RAM crisis by fixing memory prices and supply

Cue discussion of which activities hawks ordinarily do or don't do, as you'd expect

A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

The trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

"But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do."

You know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which currently looks likely to last until at least 2028.

Today, Team Cherry has announced the release date of its first DLC expansion for Hollow Knight: Silksong, and it's really good news, because it's completely free!

#4001. New Phantom Blade Zero PS5 Update Brings Features, Upgrades, and Fixes

Phantom Blade Zero studio S-Game has announced the game's next PS5 patch will arrive this Saturday, 28th November 2026, weighing in at around 7GB.

It's already posted the patch notes ahead of pushing the PS5 update live at the weekend, and they reveal new features, technical enhancements, and bug fixes coming to the game.

The most substantial additions are two fresh features: a Combat Assist section in the settings and an Automatic Strong Camera Assist setting.

"With this option turned off, strong camera assistance applies only while you are attacking an enemy. At other times, the camera makes only minor adjustments."

On the technical front, the amount of video memory and system memory the title uses has been reduced, which should improve the performance of cutscenes and general gameplay in snow-covered areas. Performance in "certain areas and boss fights" has then been enhanced, and you should see less stuttering after applying the PS5 update.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A 17-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a year was rescued and returned home by the FBI after a friend she made while playing Among Us, and his mother, were able to track down her location and pass it along to law enforcement.

Landon Tresp told the BBC that he and the anonymous girl "kind of just clicked" when they started chatting online while playing Among Us. She eventually told Tresp she was a runaway who'd been held against her will for more than a year. After learning more, Tresp, 16, told his mother, Khristina, about the exchange; she was initially suspicious, but after speaking with the girl directly on Discord and reading reports of her disappearance, she took action, asking for a piece of mail or document with a full name on it, which the girl provided.

With that, Khristina began digging into tax and property records to find relevant addresses, which she then used to find photos on real estate sites. She showed the photos to the missing girl on Discord, who picked out the one where she was being held; with that information in hand, Khristina contacted the girl's mother on social media and spoke to her briefly on the telephone, and also received a call from the FBI asking if she could confirm that the girl was still alive.

"I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her'," Khristina told the BBC. "And she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'."

The kidnapped girl contacted Khristina the following morning, after her alleged captor, 39-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel, had left the house. In a conversation monitored by the FBI, she said she'd met Harmel on social media, where he'd pretended to be disabled and offered to pay her to help him get from Utah to Oregon. When he picked her up, however, he threw her phone into a river, then drove her to Oregon.

The girl told Khristina that she was kept in his basement and forced to sleep against the wall in his bed, while he kept a knife under his pillow to prevent escape. He gave her a mobile phone that wasn't able to make calls but could connect to wifi, which is how she was able to play online and eventually reach out for help.

While Harmel was out, law enforcement began monitoring his street and house; when the moment came, police had Khristina tell the victim that it was time to make her escape. She was able to leave the house safely and into the custody of state troopers, while Harmel was subsequently arrested and charged with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

A social media post by the Salt Lake City FBI confirmed the outcome, although the crucial role played by Landon and Khristina Tresp was omitted: It says only that "the FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the US and in other countries."

A separate Department of Justice press release, however, acknowledges that "on Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025."

Khristina and Landon have remained in daily contact with the girl they helped rescue, and they're trying to arrange an in-person meetup as well. "Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina said. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away. She's doing great for what she's gone through."
